\uses{Complexity.clPlacedAction, Complexity.clRecClockIndex, Complexity.clRecFields, Complexity.clRecRowSelect, Complexity.clRecState, Complexity.clRecTrackSelect, Complexity.clRowTM, Complexity.clTrackTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction}
For a source machine, the recorder cycles through four phases: it copies the current row of movement counters onto the record, tests the unary clock, releases exactly one tracked source step with its counter updates, and returns to row copying; when the clock is exhausted it enters a completed live control. The current row is stored before the clock test, so both the initial and the final rows are present, and every counter and copy transition lies outside source time.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Whole recorder configuration]
\lean{Complexity.clRecCfg}
\label{Complexity.clRecCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clRecFields, Complexity.clRecState, Complexity.clRecTM, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks}
For a recorder control, a source configuration, movement counts, a stored record, a clock budget $T$, and a logical time $t$, the recorder configuration holds every movement counter in canonical binary at head zero, the actual record prefix with its head at the record length, the unary clock with its head at $t$, and the complete virtual reference bank of buffer and source tapes; only the record and clock heads may be away from zero.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Configuration frame during row copying]
\lean{Complexity.clRec_row_frame}
\label{Complexity.clRec_row_frame}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacedCfg, Complexity.clRecCfg, Complexity.clRecFields, Complexity.clRecRowSelect, Complexity.clRecState, Complexity.clRowCfg, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean work-tape symbols, and let $x$ and
$y$ be finite Boolean words. Let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $y$, let $b$ be
a Boolean value, let $n$ assign a natural number to each of the $(1+M.k)+(1+M.k)$
fields, let $record$ be a finite Boolean word, and let $T,t$ be natural numbers. For
each index $i$ among the $(1+M.k)+(1+M.k)+1$ row positions and each copier control $q$
among five possibilities, placing the row configuration on the selected tapes of the
recorder configuration, with state corresponding to the source state, $b$, and row state
$(i,q)$, gives exactly the recorder configuration in that state.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Invariance of the inactive row frame]
\lean{Complexity.clRec_row_inactive}
\label{Complexity.clRec_row_inactive}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacedCfg, Complexity.clRecCfg, Complexity.clRecFields, Complexity.clRecRowSelect, Complexity.clRecState, Complexity.clRowTM, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, and let $x$ and $y$
be Boolean words. Let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $y$, let $b$ be a Boolean
tag, and let $n$ assign a natural number to each of the $2(1+M.k)$ counter fields.
Choose two record words, two control states of the row-copying machine with $2(1+M.k)$
work tapes, natural numbers $T$ and $t$, and a configuration $z$ of that row-copying
machine on input $x$. Relocating $z$ into the row's designated tapes while retaining the
other tape contents and head positions gives the same configuration for either choice of
record word and row control state.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Copying a counter row]
\lean{Complexity.clRec_copy}
\label{Complexity.clRec_copy}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlaced_run, Complexity.clRecCfg, Complexity.clRecFields, Complexity.clRecRowSelect, Complexity.clRecState, Complexity.clRecTM, Complexity.clRec_row_frame, Complexity.clRec_row_inactive, Complexity.clRowCfg, Complexity.clRowPrefix, Complexity.clRowTM, Complexity.clRow_first, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols and $M.k$ work tapes,
and let $x$ and $y$ be finite Boolean words. For any configuration $c$ of $M$ on input
$y$, Boolean tag $b$, family of natural numbers $n$ indexed by $F=2(1+M.k)$ fields,
record word, and natural numbers $T,t,W$ such that the binary representation of every
$n_i$ has length at most $W$, there is a number of steps $s\le F(3W+4)+1$ after which
the recorder, started from $c$ and the tag $b$, is in its clock-test control with the
source configuration and the values $T,t$ unchanged, and with the record extended by the
concatenation, in field order, of the self-delimiting encodings of the binary
representations of the $n_i$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Disjoint coordinate embeddings]
\lean{Complexity.clLeft_ne_right}
\label{Complexity.clLeft_ne_right}
\leanok
\difficulty{2}
For natural numbers $a,b$, every $i\in\{0,\ldots,a-1\}$ and $j\in\{0,\ldots,b-1\}$ have
distinct images in $\{0,\ldots,a+b-1\}$ under the embeddings of the first and second
coordinate blocks, respectively.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Disjoint Embedded Slots]
\lean{Complexity.clRight_ne_left}
\label{Complexity.clRight_ne_left}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clLeft_ne_right}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $a,b$, every $j\in\mathrm{Fin}(b)$ and $i\in\mathrm{Fin}(a)$ give
distinct positions in $\mathrm{Fin}(a+b)$ when $j$ is embedded after the first $a$
positions and $i$ is embedded among the first $a$ positions.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Clock-Test Transition]
\lean{Complexity.clRec_tick}
\label{Complexity.clRec_tick}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clLeft_ne_right, Complexity.clRecCfg, Complexity.clRecClockIndex, Complexity.clRecFields, Complexity.clRecTM, Complexity.clRight_ne_left, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite-state Boolean Turing machine, let $x,y$ be Boolean words, and let
$c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $y$. Choose a Boolean tag $b$, a family of
natural-number movement counts $n$, a record word, and natural numbers $T,t$ with $t<T$.
One step of the recorder machine from the clock-test phase of the corresponding recorder
configuration advances the clock head from position $t$ to $t+1$ and enters the
source-release phase, leaving the other configuration data unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Exhausted clock dispatches to completion]
\lean{Complexity.clRec_stop}
\label{Complexity.clRec_stop}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clRecCfg, Complexity.clRecClockIndex, Complexity.clRecFields, Complexity.clRecTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean symbols, and let $x$ and $y$ be
Boolean words. For any configuration $c$ of $M$ on input $y$, Boolean tag $b$, function
$n$ assigning a natural number to each of the recorder’s counter fields, Boolean word
$record$, and natural number $T$, one step of the recorder from its clock-test control,
with clock time $T$, produces its completion control configuration, preserving $c$, $n$,
$record$, and $T$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Tracking Configuration Relocation]
\lean{Complexity.clRec_track_frame}
\label{Complexity.clRec_track_frame}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacedCfg, Complexity.clRecCfg, Complexity.clRecFields, Complexity.clRecState, Complexity.clRecTrackSelect, Complexity.clRefCfg, Complexity.clTrackCfg, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a finite-state Boolean Turing machine, let $x,y$ be Boolean words, and choose
a source configuration $c$ on input $y$, a Boolean tag $b$, a movement-count family $n$,
a record word, and natural numbers $T,t$. Relocating the canonical tracking
configuration determined by $c,b,n$ into the recorder's tracking slots, using the
recorder configuration's remaining tapes and head positions, gives exactly the recorder
configuration in its tracking phase.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Inactive Tracking Projection]
\lean{Complexity.clRec_track_inactive}
\label{Complexity.clRec_track_inactive}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacedCfg, Complexity.clRecCfg, Complexity.clRecFields, Complexity.clRecState, Complexity.clRecTrackSelect, Complexity.clTrackTM, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a finite-state Boolean Turing machine, let $x,y$ be Boolean words, and choose
two source configurations $c,c'$ on input $y$, two Boolean tags $b,b'$, two
movement-count families $n,n'$, a record word, natural numbers $T,t$, and any tracking
configuration $z$ on input $x$. The projections of $z$ into the recorder's tracking
slots agree when formed from either recorder layout determined by these choices.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Releasing a relocated subroutine]
\lean{Complexity.clSlot_release}
\label{Complexity.clSlot_release}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clSlotAction, Complexity.clSlotCfg, Complexity.clSlot_apply, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
Suppose a host control acts, on all reads, as the relocation of a smaller machine's transition at a fixed local state $q$, through a tape injection whose selection is a left inverse. Then one host step from the relocated configuration of any local configuration in state $q$, with its control replaced by that release control, equals the relocation of one local step. Executing the first action before observing any return guard handles equal entry and exit controls.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[One recorded source transition]
\lean{Complexity.clRec_advance}
\label{Complexity.clRec_advance}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clAdvance, Complexity.clMoves, Complexity.clPlacedCfg, Complexity.clPlaced_release, Complexity.clPlaced_run, Complexity.clRecCfg, Complexity.clRecFields, Complexity.clRecState, Complexity.clRecTM, Complexity.clRecTrackSelect, Complexity.clRec_track_frame, Complexity.clRec_track_inactive, Complexity.clTrackCfg, Complexity.clTrackTM, Complexity.clTrack_round, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.VirtualTag, Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machine, let $x,y$ be Boolean words, and let
$c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $y$. Suppose a Boolean tag $b$ correctly marks
the boundary position of $c$'s input head, and let $n$ be a family of natural-number
movement counts, indexed by the fields of a stored row, such that each count's binary
representation has length at most $W$. For any record word and natural numbers $T,t,W$,
there are a natural number $s \le 2W+5$ and a Boolean tag $b'$ correctly marking the
input-head position after one step of $M$, such that the recorder, started in its
source-release control with configuration $c$, counts $n$, record, clock budget $T$, and
logical time $t$, reaches its next row-copy control with source configuration $M(c)$,
counts advanced by one on exactly the counters selected by that transition's signed head
movements, and the same record, clock budget, and logical time.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Recorder invariant through a finite horizon]
\lean{Complexity.clRec_prefix}
\label{Complexity.clRec_prefix}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCounts, Complexity.clCounts_bound, Complexity.clCounts_succ, Complexity.clElapsed_width, Complexity.clRecCfg, Complexity.clRecFields, Complexity.clRecTM, Complexity.clRec_advance, Complexity.clRec_copy, Complexity.clRec_tick, Complexity.clRecords, Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.VirtualTag, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step'}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ and $y$ be
Boolean words, and let $T$ be a natural number. For every natural number $j\le T$, there
are a natural number $s\le j\bigl(F(3T+4)+2T+7\bigr)$ and a Boolean tag $b$, where
$F=2(1+M.k)$, such that the source machine's input-head position at time $j$ satisfies
the boundary-tag condition for $b$, and the recorder run for $s$ steps from its prepared
initial configuration equals the configuration encoding the source machine's
configuration at time $j$, the movement counts at time $j$, the record accumulated
through time $j$, and logical time $j$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Completion of trajectory recording]
\lean{Complexity.clRec_complete}
\label{Complexity.clRec_complete}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCounts, Complexity.clCounts_bound, Complexity.clElapsed_width, Complexity.clRecCfg, Complexity.clRecFields, Complexity.clRecTM, Complexity.clRec_copy, Complexity.clRec_prefix, Complexity.clRec_stop, Complexity.clRecords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step'}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean work-tape alphabet, let $x$ and
$y$ be Boolean words, and let $T$ be a nonnegative integer. Write $F=2(1+M.k)$ for the
number of movement-count fields. Starting with the recorder on physical input $x$, its
source machine in the initial state with input $y$, all counts zero, an empty record,
clock budget $T$, and logical time zero, there is a number of steps $s$ with $s\le
(T+1)(F(3T+4)+2T+7)$ after which the recorder is in its completed control. Its source
configuration is the configuration of $M$ after $T$ steps on $y$, its counts are the
recursively advanced counts at time $T$, and its record is the concatenation of the
encoded rows for times $0$ through $T$; its clock budget and logical time are both $T$,
and its physical output is empty.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Prepared recorder initialization]
\lean{Complexity.clRec_prepared}
\label{Complexity.clRec_prepared}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clRecCfg, Complexity.clRecFields, Complexity.clRecTM, Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ and $y$ be
Boolean words, and let $T$ be a natural number. The configuration formed from the
recorder's initial control, empty counter words and record, a clock containing $T$ true
bits, the word $y$, and blank source work tapes is exactly the recorder configuration
encoding the source machine's initial configuration on $y$, zero movement counts, an
empty record, and logical time zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Quadratic recording-work bound]
\lean{Complexity.clRec_cost_bound}
\label{Complexity.clRec_cost_bound}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clRecFields, Turing.FinTM}
\difficulty{3}
For every finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and every natural number
$T$, let $F$ be the number of movement-count fields per stored row, with one positive
and one negative counter for each head, including the input head. Then
$(T+1)(F(3T+4)+2T+7) \le (4F+7)(T+1)^2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Numeric value of a Boolean digit]
\lean{Complexity.clBit}
\label{Complexity.clBit}
\leanok
A Boolean digit has numeric value one when true and zero when false.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Little-endian value of a binary word]
\lean{Complexity.clNum}
\label{Complexity.clNum}
\leanok
The value of an arbitrary little-endian bit list is obtained by folding the binary digit operation over its bits, so padded words with trailing zeros are included.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Value of a natural number's binary representation]
\lean{Complexity.clNum_bits}
\label{Complexity.clNum_bits}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clNum}
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$, the little-endian value of the binary representation of
$n$ is $n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Value from the first bit and tail]
\lean{Complexity.clNum_head}
\label{Complexity.clNum_head}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clBit, Complexity.clNum}
\difficulty{2}
For every finite bit string $w$, its little-endian value equals twice the little-endian
value of its tail plus the numeric value of its first bit, taking the first bit to be
$0$ when $w$ is empty.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[One binary addition column]
\lean{Complexity.clAddColumn}
\label{Complexity.clAddColumn}
\leanok
For a carry bit and two addend bits, the addition column's low result bit is the exclusive or of the three inputs, and its outgoing carry is the majority of the three inputs.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Binary addition column identity]
\lean{Complexity.clAddColumn_value}
\label{Complexity.clAddColumn_value}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clAddColumn, Complexity.clBit}
\difficulty{2}
For Boolean bits $c,u,v$, let the low result bit be their exclusive-or and let the
outgoing carry be their majority bit. Their numeric values satisfy
$\operatorname{val}(u)+\operatorname{val}(v)+\operatorname{val}(c)=2\operatorname{val}(\text{outgoing
carry})+\operatorname{val}(\text{low result bit})$, where a true bit has value $1$ and a
false bit has value $0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Comparator register update]
\lean{Complexity.clCmpUpdate}
\label{Complexity.clCmpUpdate}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clAddColumn}
Given three Boolean registers, two running carries and an equality flag, and the four scanned column bits, the updated registers are obtained by feeding each pair of bits through its own addition column: the two outgoing carries are stored, and the equality flag is conjoined with the comparison of the two low result bits.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Comparator invariant]
\lean{Complexity.clCmpPred}
\label{Complexity.clCmpPred}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clBit, Complexity.clNum}
For comparator registers and four remaining high words, the invariant states that the equality flag is still set and that the value of the first pair of words plus the first carry equals the value of the second pair plus the second carry, given that all earlier low digits matched.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Comparator invariant under one-column update]
\lean{Complexity.clCmpUpdate_spec}
\label{Complexity.clCmpUpdate_spec}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clAddColumn, Complexity.clAddColumn_value, Complexity.clBit, Complexity.clCmpPred, Complexity.clCmpUpdate, Complexity.clNum, Complexity.clNum_head}
\difficulty{5}
Let $q$ be a triple of Boolean registers, with two carry bits and an equality flag, and
let $w_0,w_1,w_2,w_3$ be finite little-endian binary words. The comparator invariant for
$q$ on the four words holds if and only if it holds after one column update on the four
word tails, using their first bits (or zero when a word is empty) as the scanned column.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Comparator control after scanned columns]
\lean{Complexity.clCmpOrbit}
\label{Complexity.clCmpOrbit}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCmpUpdate}
For four words, the comparator control starts with clear carries and a set equality flag, and after $j+1$ columns is the register update applied to the control after $j$ columns, reading the four bits at position $j$ with blanks treated as absent.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Comparator invariant after scanned columns]
\lean{Complexity.clCmpOrbit_spec}
\label{Complexity.clCmpOrbit_spec}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clBit, Complexity.clCmpOrbit, Complexity.clCmpPred, Complexity.clCmpUpdate_spec, Complexity.clNum}
\difficulty{3}
Let $w_0,w_1,w_2,w_3$ be finite little-endian binary words and let $j$ be a natural
number. After $j$ columns have been scanned, the comparator invariant on the control
registers and the words with their first $j$ bits dropped holds if and only if
$\operatorname{val}(w_0)+\operatorname{val}(w_1)=\operatorname{val}(w_2)+\operatorname{val}(w_3)$,
where $\operatorname{val}$ denotes the little-endian binary value.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Maximum width of the compared words]
\lean{Complexity.clCmpSize}
\label{Complexity.clCmpSize}
\leanok
For four input words, the comparator size is the maximum of their four lengths; it is used only in the runtime accounting.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Bound on Each Word Length]
\lean{Complexity.clCmp_width}
\label{Complexity.clCmp_width}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCmpSize}
\difficulty{1}
For any four Boolean words and any one of their four indices, the length of the word at
that index is at most the maximum of the four word lengths.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The common boundary of four words]
\lean{Complexity.clCmp_blank}
\label{Complexity.clCmp_blank}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCmpSize}
\difficulty{1}
For any four finite Boolean words and any position $j\in\mathbb N$, all four words have
no symbol at position $j$ exactly when their maximum length is at most $j$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Final comparator verdict]
\lean{Complexity.clCmpVerdict}
\label{Complexity.clCmpVerdict}
\leanok
At the common right boundary, the verdict is true exactly when the equality flag is still set and the two final carry bits agree.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Boolean digits are determined by their values]
\lean{Complexity.clBit_eq}
\label{Complexity.clBit_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clBit}
\difficulty{2}
For Boolean digits $a$ and $b$, their numeric values—one for true and zero for false—are
equal if and only if $a=b$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The comparator verdict detects equal sums]
\lean{Complexity.clCmpVerdict_spec}
\label{Complexity.clCmpVerdict_spec}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clBit_eq, Complexity.clCmpOrbit, Complexity.clCmpOrbit_spec, Complexity.clCmpPred, Complexity.clCmpSize, Complexity.clCmpVerdict, Complexity.clCmp_width, Complexity.clNum}
\difficulty{3}
For any four finite Boolean words $w_0,w_1,w_2,w_3$, the comparator’s verdict after
scanning their common maximum width is true exactly when the little-endian values
satisfy
$\operatorname{val}(w_0)+\operatorname{val}(w_1)=\operatorname{val}(w_2)+\operatorname{val}(w_3)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Native four-word comparator]
\lean{Complexity.clCmpTM}
\label{Complexity.clCmpTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCmpUpdate, Complexity.clCmpVerdict, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction}
A machine with four work tapes scans four read-only words in lockstep, feeding each column through the finite addition tables, then rewinds all four heads to zero and idles in a live control carrying the Boolean verdict. No word is modified and nothing is physically emitted.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Comparator configuration]
\lean{Complexity.clCmpCfg}
\label{Complexity.clCmpCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCmpTM, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
For an input word, an input position, a comparator control, four stored words, and a common head position, the comparator configuration holds each word on its own buffer tape with all four heads aligned and empty output.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[The comparator reads the aligned word symbols]
\lean{Complexity.clCmp_read}
\label{Complexity.clCmp_read}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCmpCfg, Complexity.clCmpTM, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols}
\difficulty{1}
For any Boolean input word, any valid input-head position, any comparator control, four
finite Boolean words, and any natural-number position $j$, the four symbols read by the
aligned work-tape heads are exactly the symbols at position $j$ in the respective words,
with absent symbols represented by blanks.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[One comparator step scans the next column]
\lean{Complexity.clCmp_forward_step}
\label{Complexity.clCmp_forward_step}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCmpCfg, Complexity.clCmpOrbit, Complexity.clCmpSize, Complexity.clCmpTM, Complexity.clCmp_blank, Complexity.clCmp_read, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{3}
Let $x$ be a finite Boolean input word, let $p$ be a valid input-head position for $x$,
and let $w_0,w_1,w_2,w_3$ be finite Boolean words. For any $j\in\mathbb{N}$ strictly
less than the maximum of their lengths, one step of the four-tape comparator from the
configuration whose control is the state after $j$ columns and whose four tape heads are
at position $j$ gives the configuration with control after $j+1$ columns and all four
tape heads at position $j+1$, leaving the input-head position and tape contents
unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The comparator’s aligned forward scan]
\lean{Complexity.clCmp_forward}
\label{Complexity.clCmp_forward}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCmpCfg, Complexity.clCmpOrbit, Complexity.clCmpSize, Complexity.clCmpTM, Complexity.clCmp_forward_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step'}
\difficulty{3}
For any Boolean input word, any valid input-head position, and four finite Boolean
words, running the comparator for $j$ steps from its initial scanning configuration
reaches the scanning control after $j$ columns, with all work-tape heads at position
$j$, whenever $j$ is at most the maximum word length.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The comparator begins rewinding at the boundary]
\lean{Complexity.clCmp_finish_scan}
\label{Complexity.clCmp_finish_scan}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCmpCfg, Complexity.clCmpOrbit, Complexity.clCmpSize, Complexity.clCmpTM, Complexity.clCmpVerdict, Complexity.clCmp_blank, Complexity.clCmp_read, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{3}
For any Boolean input word, any valid input-head position, and any four finite Boolean
words, one step from the scanning control after the common maximum width changes the
control to the rewind state carrying the final verdict, moves every work-tape head to
one position before that width, and leaves the stored words and other configuration data
unchanged. This also holds when all four words are empty.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Rewinding the Comparator Heads]
\lean{Complexity.clCmp_rewind}
\label{Complexity.clCmp_rewind}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCmpCfg, Complexity.clCmpSize, Complexity.clCmpTM, Complexity.clCmp_blank, Complexity.clCmp_read, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{4}
For every Boolean input word $x$, every input-head position $p$ among its $|x|+2$
allowed positions, four Boolean words $w_0,w_1,w_2,w_3$, and Boolean verdict $b$, let
$m$ be the maximum of their lengths. For each natural number $j\le m$, starting the
comparator in its rewinding control with all four work-head positions at $j-1$ and
running it for $j+1$ steps yields the configuration with completed control carrying $b$,
all four heads at zero, the same words on the tapes, the same input-head position, and
empty output.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Exact Comparator Runtime]
\lean{Complexity.clCmp_run}
\label{Complexity.clCmp_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCmpCfg, Complexity.clCmpOrbit, Complexity.clCmpSize, Complexity.clCmpTM, Complexity.clCmpVerdict, Complexity.clCmp_finish_scan, Complexity.clCmp_forward, Complexity.clCmp_rewind, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step}
\difficulty{3}
For every Boolean input word $x$, every valid input-head position $p$, and every four
Boolean words $w_0,w_1,w_2,w_3$, let $m$ be the maximum of their lengths. Starting in
the comparator's initial control with all work-head positions at zero and running for
$2m+2$ steps yields the completed control carrying the comparator's final verdict after
processing $m$ columns, with the work words unchanged, all work heads at zero, the
input-head position unchanged, and output empty.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Completed comparator configurations are fixed]
\lean{Complexity.clCmp_idle}
\label{Complexity.clCmp_idle}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCmpTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{3}
For any Boolean input word, any comparator configuration, and any Boolean value $b$, if
the configuration’s control is the completed control carrying $b$, one comparator step
leaves the entire configuration unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The comparator reaches its completed verdict]
\lean{Complexity.clCmp_first}
\label{Complexity.clCmp_first}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCmpCfg, Complexity.clCmpOrbit, Complexity.clCmpSize, Complexity.clCmpTM, Complexity.clCmpVerdict, Complexity.clCmpVerdict_spec, Complexity.clCmp_idle, Complexity.clCmp_run, Complexity.clNum, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero}
\difficulty{5}
For any Boolean input word, any valid input-head position, four finite Boolean words,
and any natural number $W$ bounding all four lengths, there are a time $t$ and a Boolean
value $b$ such that $0<t\le 2W+2$, and $b$ is true exactly when the sum of the first two
words’ values equals the sum of the last two. At every time $j<t$, the machine is not in
a completed control; at time $t$, it is in the completed control carrying $b$, with the
original words intact and all work-tape heads at zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Counts match scheduled positions]
\lean{Complexity.clCounts_schedule}
\label{Complexity.clCounts_schedule}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCounts, Complexity.clCounts_positions, Complexity.clPositions, Complexity.clSigned, Complexity.inputPosAt, Complexity.workPosAt, Turing.FinTM}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, and let $m,t$ be natural
numbers. On input consisting of $m$ false bits, the signed count at the input coordinate
at time $t$, plus one, equals the input-head position after $t$ steps. For every work
tape, its signed count at time $t$ equals that tape's head position after $t$ steps on
the same input.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Packing a list of fields]
\lean{Complexity.clFields}
\label{Complexity.clFields}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairEncode}
A list of binary words is packed by encoding each word as a self-delimiting doubled-bit field, the same separators as the native copier, concatenated in order; empty binary zero fields are preserved and no fixed width is assumed.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Appending to a paired word]
\lean{Complexity.clPair_append}
\label{Complexity.clPair_append}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
For all Boolean words $a,b,c$, appending $c$ to the encoding of the pair $(a,b)$ gives
the encoding of $(a,b\text{ followed by }c)$; that is, $\langle a,b\rangle c=\langle
a,bc\rangle$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Packing Preserves Concatenation]
\lean{Complexity.clFields_append}
\label{Complexity.clFields_append}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clFields, Complexity.clPair_append}
\difficulty{3}
For any two finite lists of Boolean words $a$ and $b$, packing their concatenation gives
the concatenation of their packed encodings.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Row Prefix as Packed Fields]
\lean{Complexity.clRowPrefix_fields}
\label{Complexity.clRowPrefix_fields}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clFields, Complexity.clFields_append, Complexity.clRowPrefix}
\difficulty{3}
Let $l$ be a natural number and let $w$ assign a finite Boolean word to each of the $l$
coordinates. For every natural number $j\le l$, the stored row prefix of length $j$
equals the packed encoding of the first $j$ words in coordinate order.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Sequential field parser]
\lean{Complexity.clReadFields}
\label{Complexity.clReadFields}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairDecode}
Given a count $n$ and a bit stream, the parser repeatedly decodes one self-delimiting field, returning after $n$ fields the list of decoded words together with the exact remaining suffix; malformed streams yield no result.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Native two-tape field reader]
\lean{Complexity.clReadTM}
\label{Complexity.clReadTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clTwo, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction}
A machine with a read-only stream tape and a target tape consumes one aligned doubled-bit field: it reads each stream bit into finite control, checks the repeated bit, overwrites one target cell per decoded bit, detects the false-true separator, rewinds only the target head, and idles in a completed control. Its contract assumes the old target is no longer than the decoded field, as holds for movement counts read in increasing source-time order.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Stream-reader configuration]
\lean{Complexity.clReadCfg}
\label{Complexity.clReadCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clReadTM, Complexity.clTwo, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
For an input word, an input position, a reader control, a stream word, a target word, and independent stream and target cursors, the reader configuration holds the stream and target as buffers with the given heads; physical input and output are fixed.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Decoding a doubled bit]
\lean{Complexity.clRead_pair}
\label{Complexity.clRead_pair}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCountTape_eq, Complexity.clCountTape_write, Complexity.clReadCfg, Complexity.clReadTM, Complexity.clTwo, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ be a Boolean input word and $p$ a valid input-head position. For arbitrary
Boolean words $u,r,v,o$ and a bit $b$, initialize the reader in its scanning control
with stream $u ++ [b,b] ++ r$, target $v ++ o$, and stream and target heads at positions
$|u|$ and $|v|$, respectively. After two steps, the reader is again in its scanning
control; the stream is unchanged, its head is at $|u|+2$, the target is $v ++ b ::
o.tail$, and its head is at $|v|+1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Forward decoding of a paired field]
\lean{Complexity.clRead_forward}
\label{Complexity.clRead_forward}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clReadCfg, Complexity.clReadTM, Complexity.clRead_pair, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ and $w$ be bit words, let $p$ be an input-head position among the $|x|+2$
positions, and let $\mathrm{pre},\mathrm{tail},\mathrm{written},\mathrm{old}$ be bit
words. Starting with the reader in its initial control state, with stream
$\mathrm{pre}\,\langle w,\mathrm{tail}\rangle$ and target
$\mathrm{written}\,\mathrm{old}$, after $2|w|$ steps its stream and control state are
unchanged, while the target is $\mathrm{written}\,w\,\mathrm{drop}_{|w|}(\mathrm{old})$.
The stream cursor has advanced from $|\mathrm{pre}|$ to $|\mathrm{pre}|+2|w|$, and the
target cursor from $|\mathrm{written}|$ to $|\mathrm{written}|+|w|$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Consuming the separator]
\lean{Complexity.clRead_separator}
\label{Complexity.clRead_separator}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clReadCfg, Complexity.clReadTM, Complexity.clTwo, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{4}
For any Boolean input word $x$, valid input-head position $p$, Boolean lists $u,r,w$,
start the reader in its initial scanning control with stream $u ++
[\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}] ++ r$, target $w$, stream head at $|u|$, and target head
at $|w|$. After two steps it is in the rewind control, with the stream unchanged and its
head at $|u|+2$, and target head at $|w|-1$ (natural-number subtraction).
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Rewinding the target head]
\lean{Complexity.clRead_rewind}
\label{Complexity.clRead_rewind}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clReadCfg, Complexity.clReadTM, Complexity.clTwo, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{4}
For any Boolean input word $x$, valid input-head position $p$, stream, target word $w$,
integer stream cursor $s$, and natural number $j \le |w|$, start the reader in its
rewind control with target head at $j-1$. After $j+1$ steps it is in the completed
control, with stream and target unchanged, stream cursor $s$, and target head at zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Parsing a complete encoded field]
\lean{Complexity.clRead_run}
\label{Complexity.clRead_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clReadCfg, Complexity.clReadTM, Complexity.clRead_forward, Complexity.clRead_rewind, Complexity.clRead_separator, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
For any Boolean input word $x$, valid input-head position $p$, Boolean lists $u,w,r,o$
with $|o| \le |w|$, start the reader in its initial scanning control with stream $u ++
\langle w,r\rangle$, target $o$, stream head at $|u|$, and target head at zero. After
$3|w|+3$ steps it is in the completed control, with target $w$, stream head at
$|u|+2|w|+2$, target head at zero, and the stream unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Length of the trajectory prefix]
\lean{Complexity.clRecords_length}
\label{Complexity.clRecords_length}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCounts, Complexity.clCounts_bound, Complexity.clElapsed_width, Complexity.clRecFields, Complexity.clRecords, Complexity.clRowPrefix_length, Turing.FinTM}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $y$ be a Boolean word,
and let $T$ be a natural number. For every natural number $t\le T+1$, the serialized
trajectory prefix consisting of the first $t$ rows has length at most $t$ times the
number of movement-count fields times $2T+2$; the number of fields is twice the number
of heads, including the input head.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[First Visit to an Absorbing Return State]
\lean{Complexity.clFirst}
\label{Complexity.clFirst}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
Let a Turing machine run from a configuration $start$ to a configuration $finish$ in $B$
steps. Suppose $finish$ has state $ret$, $start$ does not have state $ret$, and every
configuration with state $ret$ is unchanged by one step. Then there is a positive time
$t\le B$ such that the run reaches exactly $finish$ at time $t$, and no configuration at
any earlier time has state $ret$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Guarded state embedding on unchanged tapes]
\lean{Complexity.clMap_run}
\label{Complexity.clMap_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clSlotCfg, Complexity.clSlot_run, Turing.Action.mapState, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{2}
Suppose a host machine with the same tapes agrees, on every embedded control satisfying a guard, with a smaller machine's transition after relabeling states. Then for every start configuration and horizon $t$ whose strictly earlier controls all satisfy the guard, the host run equals the state-relabeled run of the smaller machine; all tape data is preserved exactly.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Erasing the appended bit]
\lean{Complexity.clErase_last}
\label{Complexity.clErase_last}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_append, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat}
\difficulty{3}
For every Boolean word $w$ and bit $b$, changing the tape that stores $w$ followed by
$b$ so that the cell indexed by $|w|$ is blank gives exactly the tape that stores $w$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Two-tape scratch reset machine]
\lean{Complexity.clWipeTM}
\label{Complexity.clWipeTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clTwo, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction}
A three-state machine with a stream tape and a target tape resets its scratch target: it scans the target to its right blank, erases every occupied cell on the way back to the left blank, and returns at target cell zero in an absorbing control. The stream tape and its cursor are never read or moved.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Reset seam configuration]
\lean{Complexity.clWipeCfg}
\label{Complexity.clWipeCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clTwo, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
For an input word, an input position, a reset control, arbitrary preserved stream contents with a stream head, a target word, and a target head, the reset configuration holds the stream and target as buffers with empty physical output.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Forward scan of the scratch tape]
\lean{Complexity.clWipe_forward}
\label{Complexity.clWipe_forward}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clTwo, Complexity.clWipeCfg, Complexity.clWipeTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{4}
For every Boolean input word $x$, input-head position $p$, stream word, target word $w$,
stream-head position $s$, and integer start position $j$ with $j\le |w|$, after
$|w|-j+1$ steps from control state $0$ with target head at $j$, the reset machine is in
control state $1$, with the target still equal to $w$ and its head at $|w|-1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Backward erasing pass]
\lean{Complexity.clWipe_backward}
\label{Complexity.clWipe_backward}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clErase_last, Complexity.clTwo, Complexity.clWipeCfg, Complexity.clWipeTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $p$ be an input-head position among the $|x|+2$
positions, let $s$ be an integer, and let $v$ be a Boolean stream word. For every
Boolean word $w$, running the reset machine from its erasing control with the stream
tape holding $v$ and its head at $s$, and the target tape holding $w$ with its head at
$|w|-1$, for $|w|+1$ steps yields the configuration with the same input-head position
and stream contents and head, the target tape blank with its head at zero, and the
completed control.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Exact scratch reset duration]
\lean{Complexity.clWipe_run}
\label{Complexity.clWipe_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clWipeCfg, Complexity.clWipeTM, Complexity.clWipe_backward, Complexity.clWipe_forward, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{3}
For every Boolean input word $x$, input-head position $p$, stream word, target word $w$,
and stream-head position $s$, after exactly $2|w|+2$ steps from control state $0$ with
target head at cell $0$, the reset machine is in control state $2$, with the stream
unchanged, the target erased, and the target head at cell $0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Completed reset is stationary]
\lean{Complexity.clWipe_idle}
\label{Complexity.clWipe_idle}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clWipeTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{3}
For every Boolean input word and every configuration of the reset machine whose control
state is $2$, one step of the machine leaves the entire configuration unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[First completion of a scratch reset]
\lean{Complexity.clWipe_first}
\label{Complexity.clWipe_first}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clFirst, Complexity.clWipeCfg, Complexity.clWipeTM, Complexity.clWipe_idle, Complexity.clWipe_run, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{1}
For every Boolean input word $x$, input-head position $p$, stream word, target word $w$,
and stream-head position $s$, there is an integer time $t$ with $0<t\le 2|w|+2$ such
that the reset machine, started in control state $0$ with the target head at cell $0$,
is never in control state $2$ at any time $j<t$. At time $t$ it is in control state $2$,
with the stream unchanged, the target erased, and the target head at cell $0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Unrestricted field loader]
\lean{Complexity.clFreshTM}
\label{Complexity.clFreshTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clReadTM, Complexity.clWipeTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.seamCompTM}
A two-tape machine first runs the scratch reset on its target, then dispatches once into the banked field reader on the same tapes: the old target is actually cleared before parsing, so the new field may be empty, shorter, or unrelated to the old contents. Stream positions and all reset and read transitions are charged.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Bounded reset and field loading]
\lean{Complexity.clFresh_run}
\label{Complexity.clFresh_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clFreshTM, Complexity.clReadCfg, Complexity.clReadTM, Complexity.clRead_run, Complexity.clWipeCfg, Complexity.clWipeTM, Complexity.clWipe_first, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.seamCompTM_run_ofCfg}
\difficulty{5}
For every Boolean input word $x$, valid input-head position $p$, stream prefix
$\mathrm{pre}$, field word $w$, stream tail, and old target word, there is a time $t\le
2|\mathrm{old}|+3|w|+6$ at which the unrestricted loader, started in its reset control
with stream contents $\mathrm{pre}\,\langle w,\mathrm{tail}\rangle$, stream head at
$|\mathrm{pre}|$, and target contents $\mathrm{old}$ with head at zero, reaches the
completed reading control. At that time the target contains exactly $w$ with its head at
zero, the stream head is at $|\mathrm{pre}|+2|w|+2$, and the input position, stream
contents, and empty physical output are as specified by the corresponding reader
configuration.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Completed control is stationary]
\lean{Complexity.clFresh_idle}
\label{Complexity.clFresh_idle}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clFreshTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{3}
For every Boolean input word $x$ and every configuration $c$ of the unrestricted field
loader on $x$ whose state is its completed reading control, one step of the loader
leaves the entire configuration unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[First completion of the field loader]
\lean{Complexity.clFresh_first}
\label{Complexity.clFresh_first}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clFirst, Complexity.clFreshTM, Complexity.clFresh_idle, Complexity.clFresh_run, Complexity.clReadCfg, Complexity.clWipeCfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{2}
For every Boolean input word $x$, input-head position $p$ among its $|x|+2$ positions,
stream prefix $\mathrm{pre}$, field $w$, stream tail, and old target word, there is a
time $t$ with $0<t\le 2|\mathrm{old}|+3|w|+6$ such that, at every earlier time $j<t$,
the machine is not in its completed control. At time $t$ it is in the completed reading
control, with target contents exactly $w$ and target head at zero, stream head at
$|\mathrm{pre}|+2|w|+2$, the original input position, stream contents, and input
unchanged, and empty physical output.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Tape slots of one row-load call]
\lean{Complexity.clLoadIndex}
\label{Complexity.clLoadIndex}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clTwo}
For a target field coordinate $i$ among $l$ fields, the loader's two tapes are embedded with the shared stream first, the final extra tape, and the target field second, counter tape $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Partial inverse of the row-load slots]
\lean{Complexity.clLoadSelect}
\label{Complexity.clLoadSelect}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacement, Complexity.clPlacement.permute, Complexity.clRowSelect}
For a target field coordinate $i$, the selection maps field tape $i$ back to the loader's target slot and the final stream tape back to its stream slot, leaving every other field tape unselected.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Row-load selection inverts the injection]
\lean{Complexity.clLoad_inverse}
\label{Complexity.clLoad_inverse}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clLoadIndex, Complexity.clLoadSelect, Complexity.clTwo}
\difficulty{2}
For every target field coordinate $i$ and each of the two local loader tapes, the row-load selection applied to the embedded slot returns that local tape, and the two selected tapes are physically distinct.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Sequential row loader]
\lean{Complexity.clLoadTM}
\label{Complexity.clLoadTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clFreshTM, Complexity.clLoadSelect, Complexity.clPlacedAction, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction}
For $l$ field tapes plus one shared stream tape, the sequential loader is a controller that loads a fixed row in increasing field order: for each field it runs the unrestricted loader, reset followed by parse, on that field and the stream, dispatching once after each completed field; every field clears its own target first, so repeated queries need no monotone-width assumption.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Row-loader seam configuration]
\lean{Complexity.clLoadCfg}
\label{Complexity.clLoadCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clFreshTM, Complexity.clLoadTM, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
For an input word, an input position, a field index, a loader control, field words, a stream, and a stream cursor, the row-loader seam holds every field as a buffer at head zero and the stream with its explicit cursor; the physical output is empty.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Embedding a field-loader configuration]
\lean{Complexity.clLoad_frame}
\label{Complexity.clLoad_frame}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clFreshTM, Complexity.clLoadCfg, Complexity.clLoadSelect, Complexity.clPlacedCfg, Complexity.clPlacement.permute, Complexity.clRowSelect, Complexity.clTwo, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
\difficulty{3}
Let $l$ be a natural number, let $x$ be a binary input word, and let $p$ be an
input-head position for $x$. Choose a field index $i<l$, a loader control $q$, old words
for all fields, a stream, a replacement word, and an integer cursor position $s$. Embed
the two-tape configuration whose tapes contain the stream and replacement word into the
row loader’s slots for field $i$ and the stream, using the row loader’s current tape
contents for the other slots and placing their heads at zero. The resulting
configuration is the row-loader configuration with field $i$ replaced by the replacement
word, all other fields unchanged, and the stream and cursor preserved.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Loading one row field]
\lean{Complexity.clLoad_field}
\label{Complexity.clLoad_field}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clFreshTM, Complexity.clFresh_first, Complexity.clLoadCfg, Complexity.clLoadSelect, Complexity.clLoadTM, Complexity.clLoad_frame, Complexity.clPlaced_run, Complexity.clWipeCfg, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.moveInputPos_zero, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Let $l$ be a natural number, let $x$ be a binary input word, and let $p$ be an
input-head position for $x$. Choose a field index $i<l$, old words for all $l$ fields,
and binary words $pre$, $word$, and $tail$. The row loader, started at field $i$ with
the old fields and stream $pre$ followed by the encoding of $word$ and $tail$, reaches
in a time $t$ satisfying $0<t\le 2|old_i|+3|word|+7$ a configuration in which field $i$
contains $word$, the field index is $i+1$, and the stream cursor is at position
$|pre|+2|word|+2$, with the other fields and the stream contents as specified by the
target configuration.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Partially loaded row bank]
\lean{Complexity.clLoadWords}
\label{Complexity.clLoadWords}
\leanok
For old and new field words on $l$ coordinates and a count $j$, the intermediate bank holds the new word at every coordinate below $j$ and the old word elsewhere.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Updating the next loaded coordinate]
\lean{Complexity.clLoadWords_step}
\label{Complexity.clLoadWords_step}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clLoadWords}
\difficulty{3}
Let $l\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{old}$ and $\mathrm{new}$ assign a Boolean word to
each of the $l$ coordinates, and let $i$ be one of those coordinates. Replacing
coordinate $i$ by its new word in the bank whose coordinates below $i$ hold their new
words and whose other coordinates hold their old words gives the bank whose coordinates
below $i+1$ hold their new words and whose other coordinates hold their old words.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Decomposing the packed row at a field]
\lean{Complexity.clLoad_split}
\label{Complexity.clLoad_split}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clFields, Complexity.clFields_append, Complexity.clPair_append, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $l$ be a natural number, let $w$ assign a binary word to each of the $l$ indices,
choose an index $i<l$, and let $pre$ and $tail$ be binary words. The concatenation of
$pre$, the encoding of the whole list of fields, and $tail$ equals the concatenation of
$pre$, the encodings of the fields before $i$, the encoding of field $i$ whose second
component is the encodings of the fields after $i$ followed by $tail$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Loading a prefix of the row]
\lean{Complexity.clLoad_prefix}
\label{Complexity.clLoad_prefix}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clFields, Complexity.clFields_append, Complexity.clLoadCfg, Complexity.clLoadTM, Complexity.clLoadWords, Complexity.clLoadWords_step, Complexity.clLoad_field, Complexity.clLoad_split, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Let $l$ be a natural number, let $x$ be a binary input word, and let $p$ be an
input-head position for $x$. Suppose $old$ and $new$ assign a binary word to each of the
$l$ fields, with old-word lengths at most $U$ and new-word lengths at most $W$. For any
binary prefix and trailer and every $j\le l$, the row loader started at field zero with
the old fields and the stream containing the prefix, packed new fields, and trailer
reaches in some time $t\le j(2U+3W+7)$ a configuration at field index $j$, with fields
below $j$ replaced by their new words and the rest still old, and with the stream cursor
immediately after the packed first $j$ new fields.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Completion of the row load]
\lean{Complexity.clLoad_complete}
\label{Complexity.clLoad_complete}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clFields, Complexity.clLoadCfg, Complexity.clLoadTM, Complexity.clLoadWords, Complexity.clLoad_prefix, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{2}
Let $l$ be a natural number, let $x$ be a binary input word, and let $p$ be an
input-head position among its $|x|+2$ positions. Suppose $old$ and $new$ assign a binary
word to each of the $l$ fields, with every old word of length at most $U$ and every new
word of length at most $W$. For any prefix and trailer, the row loader started at field
zero with the old fields and stream consisting of the prefix, the packed new fields, and
the trailer reaches, in some time $t\le l(2U+3W+7)$, the configuration with all fields
equal to the new fields, the field index at $l$, and the stream cursor immediately after
the packed new fields; the input position and stream contents are as specified by these
configurations.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[The completed loader state is fixed]
\lean{Complexity.clLoad_idle}
\label{Complexity.clLoad_idle}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clLoadTM, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{3}
For any natural number $l$, binary input word $x$, and configuration of the row loader
on $x$, if its state is the final field index $l$ paired with the fresh loader’s initial
reset control, then one machine step leaves the entire configuration unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[First completion of a nonempty row load]
\lean{Complexity.clLoad_first}
\label{Complexity.clLoad_first}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clFields, Complexity.clFirst, Complexity.clLoadCfg, Complexity.clLoadTM, Complexity.clLoad_complete, Complexity.clLoad_idle, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{3}
Let $l>0$, let $x$ be a binary input word, and let $p$ be an input-head position for
$x$. Suppose $old$ and $new$ assign a binary word to each of the $l$ fields, with
old-word lengths at most $U$ and new-word lengths at most $W$. For any binary prefix and
trailer, the row loader started at field zero with the old fields and the stream
containing the prefix, packed new fields, and trailer reaches the complete-row
configuration at some time $t$ with $0<t\le l(2U+3W+7)$, and at every earlier time $j<t$
its state is not the complete-row control at field index $l$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Native input copier]
\lean{Complexity.clInputTM}
\label{Complexity.clInputTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction}
A three-state machine with one work tape copies its entire native input onto the work tape, rewinds the input head against the physical left boundary with the destination head following exactly, and idles in a silent live return control.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Input-copy configuration]
\lean{Complexity.clInputCfg}
\label{Complexity.clInputCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
For an input word, a copier control, an input position, a copied prefix, and a work head, the copy configuration holds the copied prefix as a buffer with aligned heads and empty output.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Forward input-copying run]
\lean{Complexity.clInput_forward}
\label{Complexity.clInput_forward}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clInputCfg, Complexity.clInputTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_append, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.inputSymbolInner, Turing.moveInputPos_pos_of_ne_right}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ be a Boolean word. For every $j$ with $0\le j\le |x|$, after $j$ steps from the
copier configuration with input head at position $1$, empty work tape, and work head at
$0$, the machine is in its copying control with input head at position $j+1$, the first
$j$ bits of $x$ copied onto the work tape, and work head at position $j$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Rewinding the input head]
\lean{Complexity.clInput_backward}
\label{Complexity.clInput_backward}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clInputCfg, Complexity.clInputTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.FinTM.moveInputPos_neg_val, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.inputSymbolInner, Turing.moveInputPos}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ and $w$ be finite Boolean words, and let $j$ be a natural number with $j \le
|x|$. Starting in state $1$ with the input head at position $j$ and the work head at
position $j-1$, with work tape storing $w$ and empty output, the copier reaches after
$j+1$ steps the configuration in state $2$ with the input head at position $1$, the work
head at position $0$, the work tape still storing $w$, and empty output.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Complete input-copying run]
\lean{Complexity.clInput_run}
\label{Complexity.clInput_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clInputCfg, Complexity.clInputTM, Complexity.clInput_backward, Complexity.clInput_forward, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM.moveInputPos_neg_val, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
For every Boolean word $x$, after exactly $2|x|+2$ steps from the input copier’s initial
configuration on $x$, the machine is in its return control with $x$ on its work tape,
both heads at their initial positions, and empty output.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Absorbing copy-return control]
\lean{Complexity.clInput_idle}
\label{Complexity.clInput_idle}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clInputTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{3}
For every Boolean input word $x$ and every configuration $c$ of the input copier on $x$,
if $c$ is in state $2$, then one machine step leaves the entire configuration unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[First arrival at the copied-input configuration]
\lean{Complexity.clInput_first}
\label{Complexity.clInput_first}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clFirst, Complexity.clInputTM, Complexity.clInput_idle, Complexity.clInput_run, Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{1}
For every Boolean word $x$, there is a time $t$ with $0<t\le 2|x|+2$ such that the input
copier, started in its initial configuration on $x$, is not in its return control at any
earlier time $j<t$ and at time $t$ is in the return control with $x$ on its work tape,
both heads at their initial positions, and empty output.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Stream slot of the preparation copier]
\lean{Complexity.clPrepareIndex}
\label{Complexity.clPrepareIndex}
\leanok
During native preparation, the input copier's single work tape is embedded as the final stream slot of the field bank of $l + 1$ tapes.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Partial inverse of the preparation slot]
\lean{Complexity.clPrepareSelect}
\label{Complexity.clPrepareSelect}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacement, Complexity.clPlacement.trailing}
The preparation selection maps the final stream slot back to the copier's only tape and leaves every future field target inactive during the input-copy phase.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Preparation transducer]
\lean{Complexity.clPrepareTM}
\label{Complexity.clPrepareTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clInputTM, Complexity.clLoadTM, Complexity.clPlacedAction, Complexity.clPrepareSelect, Turing.Action.mapState, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction}
For $l$ field tapes plus one stream tape, the preparation machine first runs the native input copier into the stream slot, then dispatches once into the sequential row loader, which parses the fixed number of self-delimiting fields from the copied stream.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Preparation from the Initial Configuration]
\lean{Complexity.clPrepare_start}
\label{Complexity.clPrepare_start}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clInputTM, Complexity.clInput_first, Complexity.clLoadCfg, Complexity.clPlacedCfg, Complexity.clPlaced_run, Complexity.clPrepareSelect, Complexity.clPrepareTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{5}
For every $l\in\mathbb{N}$ and every Boolean input word $x$, there is a time $t\le
2|x|+3$ at which the preparation machine started on $x$ reaches the loader entry
configuration: its field tapes are blank, its stream tape contains $x$ with its head at
position zero, its input head is at position $1$, its loader counter is zero, and its
output is empty.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Completion of field preparation]
\lean{Complexity.clPrepare_complete}
\label{Complexity.clPrepare_complete}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clFields, Complexity.clLoadCfg, Complexity.clLoadTM, Complexity.clLoad_complete, Complexity.clPrepareTM, Complexity.clPrepare_start, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_mapState_of_agreeOn}
\difficulty{4}
Let $l,W\in\mathbb{N}$, let $w$ assign a Boolean word to each of the $l$ field indices,
with every word having length at most $W$, and let $\mathrm{tail}$ be any Boolean word.
Form $x$ by concatenating the packed encoding of the list of fields $w$ with
$\mathrm{tail}$. There is a time $t\le 2|x|+3+l(3W+7)$ at which the preparation machine
started on $x$ has exactly the configuration whose input head is at position $1$, whose
counter is at its final value, whose loader is in its entry state, whose field tapes
contain their respective words, and whose stream tape contains $x$ with its head at
position equal to the length of the packed fields; the output is empty.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Stationarity at the Loader Return]
\lean{Complexity.clPrepare_idle}
\label{Complexity.clPrepare_idle}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clLoadTM, Complexity.clPrepareTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{3}
For any $l\in\mathbb{N}$, input word $x$, and configuration $c$ of the preparation
machine on $x$, if the state of $c$ is the loader's final-counter return state, then one
computation step leaves the entire configuration unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[First Arrival at the Prepared Configuration]
\lean{Complexity.clPrepare_first}
\label{Complexity.clPrepare_first}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clFields, Complexity.clFirst, Complexity.clLoadCfg, Complexity.clPrepareTM, Complexity.clPrepare_complete, Complexity.clPrepare_idle, Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom}
\difficulty{2}
Let $l,W\in\mathbb{N}$, let $w_0,\ldots,w_{l-1}$ be Boolean words of length at most $W$,
and let $\mathrm{tail}$ be any Boolean word; let $x$ be the packed encoding of the row
followed by the trailer. There is a time $t\le 2|x|+3+l(3W+7)$ with $t>0$ such that the
preparation machine started on $x$ has the specified loading configuration at time $t$,
and at every earlier time $j<t$ its state is not the loader's final-counter entry state.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial-time packing of function values]
\lean{Complexity.clNative_fields}
\label{Complexity.clNative_fields}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.clFields, Complexity.clNative_linear, Complexity.clNative_pair, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_const}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\mathrm{fs}$ be a finite list of functions from binary words to binary words, and
suppose every function in the list is polynomial-time computable. Then the function
sending an input $x$ to the packed encoding of the list of values of those functions at
$x$, in list order, is polynomial-time computable.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Iterated header tail]
\lean{Complexity.clHeaderTail}
\label{Complexity.clHeaderTail}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairDecode}
For a count $j$ and an encoded nested-pair header, the $j$-th tail follows the payload projection $j$ times, with the empty word as default for malformed input; the projections are actual native scans.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Fixed header field]
\lean{Complexity.clHeaderField}
\label{Complexity.clHeaderField}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clHeaderTail, Turing.pairDecode}
For a count $j$ and an encoded nested-pair header, the $j$-th field is the first component of the $j$-th tail, with the empty word as default; selection is implemented by charged scans, not free indexing.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial-time header tails]
\lean{Complexity.clHeaderTail_native}
\label{Complexity.clHeaderTail_native}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.comp, Complexity.clHeaderTail, Complexity.clNative_linear, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_id, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairSnd}
\difficulty{2}
For every fixed nonnegative integer $j$, the function that sends a Boolean word $z$ to
the result of applying the payload projection $j$ times, using the empty word whenever a
projection is undefined, is polynomial-time computable.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial-time computation of header fields]
\lean{Complexity.clHeaderField_native}
\label{Complexity.clHeaderField_native}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.comp, Complexity.clHeaderField, Complexity.clHeaderTail_native, Complexity.clNative_linear, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_pairFst}
\difficulty{1}
For every fixed natural number $j$, the function that maps a Boolean word encoding a
nested-pair header to its $j$-th field, returning the empty word when the parsing or
field selection is undefined, is polynomial-time computable.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Prepared work words of the recorder]
\lean{Complexity.clRecWords}
\label{Complexity.clRecWords}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clRecFields, Complexity.clRecTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks}
For a source machine, virtual input $y$, and horizon $T$, the recorder's prepared work words are: empty movement counters, an empty record, a unary clock of $T$ true bits, the virtual input $y$, and blank source tapes, in the recorder's established tape layout.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Four retained header fields]
\lean{Complexity.clHeaderKeep}
\label{Complexity.clHeaderKeep}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clHeaderField}
From an encoded preparation header, the four retained fields are its first four components: the instance, the binary certificate length, the binary reference-input length, and the binary source horizon.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Recorder layout of the unpacked header]
\lean{Complexity.clHeaderLayout}
\label{Complexity.clHeaderLayout}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clHeaderField, Complexity.clHeaderKeep, Complexity.clHeaderTail, Complexity.clRecFields, Complexity.clRecTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks}
From an encoded preparation header, the full layout places blank counters, an empty record, the original fifth tail as the unary clock, and the fourth field as the virtual reference input into the recorder bank, followed by the four retained arithmetic and instance fields in a disjoint bank; the clock is the original horizon, not a guessed or enlarged one.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial-time recorder layout]
\lean{Complexity.clHeaderLayout_native}
\label{Complexity.clHeaderLayout_native}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.clFields, Complexity.clHeaderField_native, Complexity.clHeaderKeep, Complexity.clHeaderLayout, Complexity.clHeaderTail_native, Complexity.clNative_fields, Complexity.clNative_linear, Complexity.clRecTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_const, Turing.FinTM.tapeBlocks}
\difficulty{4}
For every finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet, the function that sends a
Boolean word $z$ to the self-delimiting packing of the list of fields in its recorder
layout is polynomial-time computable.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Exact recorder header layout]
\lean{Complexity.clHeaderLayout_exact}
\label{Complexity.clHeaderLayout_exact}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clHeaderField, Complexity.clHeaderKeep, Complexity.clHeaderLayout, Complexity.clHeaderTail, Complexity.clPrepHeader, Complexity.clRecWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.pairDecode_pairEncode}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $C,e,c,A,d$ be
nonnegative integers, and let $x$ be a Boolean word. Set $Q=C(|x|+1)^e$, $m=|x|+Q$, and
$T=c(A(m+1)^d+1)^2$. The recorder layout obtained from the arithmetic header encoding of
$x,Q,m,T$, an all-false word of length $m$, and a clock of $T$ true bits equals the
layout consisting of the recorder’s prepared words for that reference input and horizon,
followed by four fields: $x$, the binary representation of $Q$, the binary
representation of $m$, and the binary representation of $T$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial-Time Recorder Layout]
\lean{Complexity.clRecordArgument_native}
\label{Complexity.clRecordArgument_native}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.comp, Complexity.clFields, Complexity.clHeaderLayout, Complexity.clHeaderLayout_native, Complexity.clPrepHeader, Complexity.clPrepHeader_native, Turing.FinTM}
\difficulty{1}
For every finite-state Boolean Turing machine $M$ and natural numbers $C,e,c,A,d$, the
function sending a Boolean word $x$ to the packed encoding of the recorder layout formed
from the arithmetic preparation header with these parameters is polynomial-time
computable.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Protected slots of the recorder host]
\lean{Complexity.clRecordSelect}
\label{Complexity.clRecordSelect}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacement, Complexity.clPlacement.empty, Complexity.clPlacement.refl, Complexity.clPlacement.sum, Complexity.clRecTM, Turing.FinTM}
In the recorder host's bank, the selection maps the first slots back to the active recorder tapes and leaves the four retained header fields and the native-input buffer unselected, protecting them from recorder actions.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Injection into the recorder host]
\lean{Complexity.clRecordIndex}
\label{Complexity.clRecordIndex}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clRecTM, Turing.FinTM}
Each active recorder tape is embedded into the host bank before the four retained header fields and the final input-buffer slot.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Recorder selection inverts its injection]
\lean{Complexity.clRecord_inverse}
\label{Complexity.clRecord_inverse}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clRecTM, Complexity.clRecordIndex, Complexity.clRecordSelect, Turing.FinTM}
\difficulty{1}
For every active recorder tape coordinate, the host selection applied to the embedded coordinate returns that coordinate, with no aliasing of the protected fields.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Prepared recorder host]
\lean{Complexity.clRecordTM}
\label{Complexity.clRecordTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacedAction, Complexity.clPrepareTM, Complexity.clRecTM, Complexity.clRecordSelect, Turing.Action.mapState, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction}
The host machine runs native field preparation on the full bank, dispatches once at the prepared seam into the unchanged inclusive trajectory recorder, and then runs the recorder on its active slots while the retained header fields and input buffer stay protected; the completed recorder remains live so that later search and packing phases can be attached.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Retained configuration around the recorder]
\lean{Complexity.clRecordCfg}
\label{Complexity.clRecordCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacedCfg, Complexity.clRecTM, Complexity.clRecordSelect, Complexity.clRecordTM, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
For an input word, four retained header fields, and a recorder configuration, the host configuration is the recorder configuration embedded on the active slots, with the four header fields kept at head zero and the original encoded input kept on the final buffer with its cursor at the input's full length.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Prepared recorder configuration]
\lean{Complexity.clRecord_prepare_frame}
\label{Complexity.clRecord_prepare_frame}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clLoadCfg, Complexity.clRecCfg, Complexity.clRecTM, Complexity.clRecWords, Complexity.clRec_prepared, Complexity.clRecordCfg, Complexity.clRecordSelect, Complexity.clRecordTM, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x,y$ be Boolean
words, let $T$ be a natural number, and let $\mathrm{keep}$ assign a Boolean word to
each of four slots. The configuration obtained by replacing the loader's control with
the recorder's initial state is exactly the recorder configuration at time zero,
initialized on virtual input $y$, with all movement counters zero, empty record, clock
parameter $T$, and retained words $\mathrm{keep}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Completion of trajectory recording]
\lean{Complexity.clRecord_complete}
\label{Complexity.clRecord_complete}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCounts, Complexity.clFields, Complexity.clLoadCfg, Complexity.clPlaced_run, Complexity.clPrepareTM, Complexity.clPrepare_first, Complexity.clRecCfg, Complexity.clRecFields, Complexity.clRecTM, Complexity.clRecWords, Complexity.clRec_complete, Complexity.clRec_cost_bound, Complexity.clRecordCfg, Complexity.clRecordSelect, Complexity.clRecordTM, Complexity.clRecord_prepare_frame, Complexity.clRecords, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_mapState_of_agreeOn, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M$ be a finite-state Boolean machine, let $y$ be a Boolean word, let $T$ be a
natural number, let $(k_i)_{i<4}$ be four Boolean words, and let $W$ be a natural
number. Suppose every word among the recorder's initial tape contents for $M$, $y$, and
$T$, together with the four words $k_i$, has length at most $W$. Let $x$ be the
self-delimiting packing of those words. Then there is a time $t$ satisfying $t\le
2|x|+4+((\mathrm{recorder\ tape\ count})+4)(3W+7)+(4(\mathrm{field\ count})+7)(T+1)^2$
at which the recording machine's configuration is exactly the completed recorder
configuration: the source machine is in its configuration after $T$ steps, its movement
counts through time $T$ and all recorded rows through time $T$ are stored, and the
prescribed input and retained fields are in their designated tape locations.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Comparator words of one row query]
\lean{Complexity.clMatchWords}
\label{Complexity.clMatchWords}
\leanok
For positive and negative counter coordinates and a stored row, together with two retained target count words, the four comparator words are, in order: the row's positive count, the second target word, the first target word, and the row's negative count, exactly the cross-sum interface of the banked comparator.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Loader slots inside the search]
\lean{Complexity.clMatchLoadIndex}
\label{Complexity.clMatchLoadIndex}
\leanok
The row loader's $l + 1$ tapes are embedded into the search's $l + 5$ tapes with the candidate fields first and the record stream as the first administrative slot.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Partial inverse of the search-loader slots]
\lean{Complexity.clMatchLoadSelect}
\label{Complexity.clMatchLoadSelect}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacement, Complexity.clPlacement.empty, Complexity.clPlacement.refl, Complexity.clPlacement.sum}
The search's selection maps each candidate field and the record stream back to their loader coordinates, and leaves the two target words, the query clock, and the flag tape unselected during loading.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Search-loader selection inverts its injection]
\lean{Complexity.clMatchLoad_inverse}
\label{Complexity.clMatchLoad_inverse}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clMatchLoadIndex, Complexity.clMatchLoadSelect}
\difficulty{2}
For every loader tape coordinate, the search's loading selection applied to the embedded slot returns that coordinate, with no aliasing.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Comparator slots inside the search]
\lean{Complexity.clMatchCmpIndex}
\label{Complexity.clMatchCmpIndex}
\leanok
