For distinct positive and negative counter coordinates, the four comparator tapes are embedded as: the candidate's positive count field, the second target slot, the first target slot, and the candidate's negative count field; the injection is fixed, with no data-dependent or uncharged record lookup.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Partial inverse of the search-comparator slots]
\lean{Complexity.clMatchCmpSelect}
\label{Complexity.clMatchCmpSelect}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacement, Complexity.clPlacement.ofInverse}
The search's comparison selection maps the positive and negative candidate fields and the two target slots back to their comparator coordinates, and leaves the stream, clock, flag tape, and all other fields fixed.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Comparator selection inverts its injection]
\lean{Complexity.clMatchCmp_inverse}
\label{Complexity.clMatchCmp_inverse}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clMatchCmpIndex, Complexity.clMatchCmpSelect}
\difficulty{2}
For distinct positive and negative coordinates and each of the four comparator tapes, the search's comparison selection applied to the embedded slot returns that tape, so the call is a genuine four-tape comparison.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Control phases of the matcher]
\lean{Complexity.clMatchState}
\label{Complexity.clMatchState}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCmpTM, Complexity.clLoadTM}
The matcher's finite control is a disjoint sum of four phases: the clock test, the sequential row load, the native comparison, and the completed live return.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Native all-earlier-row matcher]
\lean{Complexity.clMatchTM}
\label{Complexity.clMatchTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCmpTM, Complexity.clLoadTM, Complexity.clMatchCmpSelect, Complexity.clMatchLoadSelect, Complexity.clMatchState, Complexity.clPlacedAction, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction}
For distinct positive and negative counter coordinates, the matcher repeatedly tests its unary query clock, loads one stored row from the record stream, compares cross-sums against two retained target words, and appends one flag per row in source-time order; when the clock is exhausted it stops before inspecting the next row, so exactly the clock's length of rows is inspected and the row at the target time is excluded.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Complete search seam]
\lean{Complexity.clMatchCfg}
\label{Complexity.clMatchCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clMatchState, Complexity.clMatchTM, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
For a matcher control, candidate fields, two immutable target count words, the record stream with an explicit cursor, a unary query clock of $N$ tokens with its head at $j$, and the stored flag prefix, the search configuration holds every binary field at head zero, the flag tape head at the flag count, and empty physical output.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Live Clock Starts a Row Query]
\lean{Complexity.clMatch_tick}
\label{Complexity.clMatch_tick}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clMatchCfg, Complexity.clMatchTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{3}
For every $l,N,j\in\mathbb{N}$, every $pos,neg\in\text{Fin}(l)$, input word, row, target
words, stream, cursor, and flag word, if $j<N$, one step of the matcher from its initial
search control enters the row-loading control at counter zero with the fresh-loader
state. The row, target words, stream, cursor, clock position, and flags are unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Exhausted Clock Stops the Matcher]
\lean{Complexity.clMatch_stop}
\label{Complexity.clMatch_stop}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clMatchCfg, Complexity.clMatchTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{3}
For every $l\in\mathbb{N}$, every $pos,neg\in\text{Fin}(l)$, input word, row, target
words, stream, cursor, clock length $N$, and flag word, if the matcher is in its initial
search control with clock position $N$, one machine step puts it in the completed
control. All tape contents and work-head positions remain as specified by that same
search configuration.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Loader Configuration Embedding]
\lean{Complexity.clMatch_load_frame}
\label{Complexity.clMatch_load_frame}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clLoadCfg, Complexity.clLoadTM, Complexity.clMatchCfg, Complexity.clMatchLoadSelect, Complexity.clMatchState, Complexity.clPlacedCfg}
\difficulty{3}
For any number $l$ of candidate fields, positive and negative coordinates in
$\text{Fin}(l)$, input word, loader state, old and new rows, target words, stream,
cursors, clock data, and flags, embedding the loader configuration into the matcher’s
loading slots gives the matcher configuration in its loading state. The embedded
configuration uses the new row and the supplied stream cursor; the target words, clock,
flags, and their head positions are those of the matcher configuration.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Loading a candidate row]
\lean{Complexity.clMatch_load}
\label{Complexity.clMatch_load}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clFields, Complexity.clLoadCfg, Complexity.clLoadTM, Complexity.clLoad_first, Complexity.clMatchCfg, Complexity.clMatchLoadSelect, Complexity.clMatchState, Complexity.clMatchTM, Complexity.clMatch_load_frame, Complexity.clPlaced_run, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.FinTM.controlAction_apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{5}
Let $l$ be a positive natural number, let $pos,neg$ be coordinates in the range of
length $l$, and choose a Boolean input word, old and new rows of Boolean words, two
target words, Boolean prefix and trailer, natural numbers $N,j,W$, and a Boolean flag
word. Suppose every word in the old and new rows has length at most $W$. Then there is a
natural number $t\le l(5W+7)+1$ such that after $t$ steps the matcher holds the new row,
its stream cursor has advanced from the prefix length by exactly the length of the
packed new row, its clock and flags are unchanged, the old row contents have been
replaced, and the matcher is in the initial comparison control.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Comparator configuration in the search frame]
\lean{Complexity.clMatch_cmp_frame}
\label{Complexity.clMatch_cmp_frame}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCmpCfg, Complexity.clCmpTM, Complexity.clMatchCfg, Complexity.clMatchCmpSelect, Complexity.clMatchState, Complexity.clMatchWords, Complexity.clPlacedCfg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $l\in\mathbb{N}$, let $pos,neg\in\{0,\ldots,l-1\}$ be distinct, let $x$ be a Boolean
input word, and choose an arbitrary comparator control state $q$, row of Boolean words,
two target words, Boolean stream, integer cursor, natural numbers $N,j$, and Boolean
flag word. Placing the four comparator tapes, initialized with the row's positive word,
the second target, the first target, and the row's negative word, into their designated
search slots, while embedding the comparator state in the comparison phase, gives
exactly the search configuration in that phase with all other tapes, head positions,
stream, cursor, clock data, and flags unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Committing a comparison flag]
\lean{Complexity.clMatch_commit}
\label{Complexity.clMatch_commit}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clMatchCfg, Complexity.clMatchTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_append, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.moveInputPos_zero}
\difficulty{3}
Let $l\in\mathbb{N}$, let $pos,neg\in\{0,\ldots,l-1\}$, and choose a Boolean input word,
verdict bit $b$, row of Boolean words, two target words, Boolean stream, integer cursor,
natural numbers $N,j$, and Boolean flag word. From the search configuration in the
comparison-finished control holding verdict $b$, one step of the matcher returns to the
clock-test control, advances the clock from $j$ to $j+1$, and appends $b$ to the flags;
the stream cursor and all other displayed data remain unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bounded signed comparison]
\lean{Complexity.clMatch_compare}
\label{Complexity.clMatch_compare}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCmpCfg, Complexity.clCmpTM, Complexity.clCmp_first, Complexity.clMatchCfg, Complexity.clMatchCmpSelect, Complexity.clMatchState, Complexity.clMatchTM, Complexity.clMatchWords, Complexity.clMatch_cmp_frame, Complexity.clMatch_commit, Complexity.clNum, Complexity.clPlaced_run, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step'}
\difficulty{5}
Let $l\in\mathbb{N}$, let $pos,neg\in\{0,\ldots,l-1\}$ be distinct, and choose a Boolean
input word, row of Boolean words, two target words, Boolean stream, integer cursor, and
natural numbers $N,j,W$. Suppose every row word and target word has length at most $W$.
Then there are a natural number $t\le 2W+3$ and a bit $b$ such that $b$ is true exactly
when the value of the row's positive word plus the second target word equals the value
of the first target word plus the row's negative word; after $t$ steps from the
comparison control, the matcher is in the clock-test control, has advanced its clock to
$j+1$, and has appended $b$ to the flags, with the other displayed data unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Generic ordered row stream]
\lean{Complexity.clRows}
\label{Complexity.clRows}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clFields}
For every family of rows of $l$ binary fields indexed by time and every count $n$, the stream of the first $n$ rows is the concatenation of the packed self-delimiting encodings of rows $0, \dots, n-1$ in order, in exactly the banked field format.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Concatenation of Row Streams]
\lean{Complexity.clRows_add}
\label{Complexity.clRows_add}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clRows}
\difficulty{3}
For any natural number $l$, any family of rows $\mathrm{row}(n,i)$ of Boolean words
indexed by $n\in\mathbb N$ and $i<l$, and all natural numbers $n,m$, the stream of the
first $n+m$ packed rows equals the stream of the first $n$ packed rows followed by the
stream of the first $m$ packed rows of the shifted family $i\mapsto\mathrm{row}(n+i,i)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Factoring a Row from the Stream]
\lean{Complexity.clRows_split}
\label{Complexity.clRows_split}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clFields, Complexity.clRows, Complexity.clRows_add}
\difficulty{3}
Let $l$ be a natural number, let $\mathrm{row}(n,i)$ be a family of Boolean words
indexed by time $n$ and coordinate $i<l$, and let $N,j$ be natural numbers with $j<N$.
For every Boolean word $u$, there is a Boolean word $v$ such that the stream of the
first $N$ rows followed by $u$ equals the stream of the first $j$ rows, followed by the
packed encoding of row $j$, followed by $v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Recorder Equals Generic Row Stream]
\lean{Complexity.clRows_records}
\label{Complexity.clRows_records}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCounts, Complexity.clRecords, Complexity.clRowPrefix_fields, Complexity.clRows, Turing.FinTM}
\difficulty{3}
For every finite Boolean Turing machine $M$, Boolean input word $y$, and natural number
$n$, the generic stream of the first $n$ rows whose fields are the binary
representations of the movement counts of $M$ on $y$ equals the recorder's serialized
trajectory prefix of $n$ rows.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Flag of one signed-position comparison]
\lean{Complexity.clMatchFlag}
\label{Complexity.clMatchFlag}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clNum}
For positive and negative coordinates, a stored row, and two target count words, the flag is true exactly when the row's positive count plus the second target value equals the first target value plus the row's negative count.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[One matcher round]
\lean{Complexity.clMatch_round}
\label{Complexity.clMatch_round}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clFields, Complexity.clMatchCfg, Complexity.clMatchFlag, Complexity.clMatchTM, Complexity.clMatch_compare, Complexity.clMatch_load, Complexity.clMatch_tick, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $l,N,j,W$ be natural numbers, and let $pos,neg\in\mathrm{Fin}(l)$ be distinct. Let
$x$ be a finite Boolean word, let $old,row:\mathrm{Fin}(l)\to\{0,1\}^*$ be rows of
Boolean words, and let $target:\mathrm{Fin}(2)\to\{0,1\}^*$ be a pair of target words.
For Boolean words $pre,tail$ and a list $flags$ of Boolean values, suppose $j<N$, every
word $old(i)$ and $row(i)$ has length at most $W$, and both target words have length at
most $W$. Then for some natural number $t\le l(5W+7)+2W+5$, after $t$ steps the matcher
is in the configuration with row $row$, stream $pre$ followed by the packed encoding of
the fields of $row$ and then $tail$, cursor at the end of that packed encoding, clock
position $j+1$, and flags equal to the original list followed by the comparison flag
determined by $row$ and $target$ at $pos$ and $neg$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Candidate bank before the next load]
\lean{Complexity.clPriorRow}
\label{Complexity.clPriorRow}
\leanok
For a row family and a time $j$, the candidate bank before loading row $j$ holds empty fields when $j = 0$ and row $j - 1$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Prefix Scan Records Comparison Flags]
\lean{Complexity.clMatch_prefix}
\label{Complexity.clMatch_prefix}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clMatchCfg, Complexity.clMatchFlag, Complexity.clMatchTM, Complexity.clMatch_round, Complexity.clPriorRow, Complexity.clRows, Complexity.clRows_split, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{5}
Let $l,N,W$ be natural numbers, let $pos,neg\in\text{Fin}(l)$ be distinct, let $x$ be a
Boolean input word, let $row_s$ be a family of $l$ Boolean words indexed by
$s\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $target_0,target_1$ be Boolean words, each of length at most
$W$. Suppose every field of each row with $s<N$ has length at most $W$. For every $j\le
N$, there is a time $t\le j\bigl(l(5W+7)+2W+5\bigr)$ at which the matcher, started with
empty candidate fields, cursor zero, and no flags, has empty candidates if $j=0$ and
otherwise holds row $j-1$; its stream cursor is the length of the packed first $j$ rows,
its clock position is $j$, and its flags, in order, are the comparison flags of rows $0$
through $j-1$. The target words remain the supplied target words.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Bounded completion of the row search]
\lean{Complexity.clMatch_complete}
\label{Complexity.clMatch_complete}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clMatchCfg, Complexity.clMatchFlag, Complexity.clMatchTM, Complexity.clMatch_prefix, Complexity.clMatch_stop, Complexity.clPriorRow, Complexity.clRows, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step'}
\difficulty{2}
Let $l\in\mathbb{N}$, let $pos,neg\in\{0,\ldots,l-1\}$ be distinct, and choose a Boolean
input word, a family of rows of Boolean words indexed by natural numbers, two target
words, natural numbers $N,W$, and a Boolean trailer. Suppose each word in each of the
first $N$ rows has length at most $W$, and each target word has length at most $W$.
There is a natural number $t\le N\bigl(l(5W+7)+2W+5\bigr)+1$ such that after $t$ steps
the matcher is in its completed control, the candidate bank holds empty words if $N=0$
and otherwise row $N-1$, the stream and targets are unchanged, the cursor is at the
length of the packed first $N$ rows, the clock is $N$, and the flags are the comparison
results for rows $0$ through $N-1$ in order.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Scheduled work-head position equality]
\lean{Complexity.clMatchFlag_schedule}
\label{Complexity.clMatchFlag_schedule}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clCounts, Complexity.clCounts_schedule, Complexity.clMatchFlag, Complexity.clNum_bits, Complexity.clSigned_eq, Complexity.clTwo, Complexity.workPosAt, Turing.FinTM}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a binary multi-tape Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let
$m,s,t\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $\tau$ be a work-tape index. For the movement-count row at
time $s$ on the all-zero input of length $m$, and two target words both taken from the
movement counts at time $t$, the comparison flag at the positive and negative slots for
$\tau$ is true exactly when the work-head positions at times $s$ and $t$ on tape $\tau$
are equal.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Optional-time code]
\lean{Complexity.clVisitCode}
\label{Complexity.clVisitCode}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairEncode}
An absent visit is encoded as the empty word; a present visit at time $s$ is encoded as an aligned separator followed by the canonical little-endian binary representation of $s$. The code is unambiguous and compact.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Code of the last marked time]
\lean{Complexity.clLastCode}
\label{Complexity.clLastCode}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clVisitCode, Turing.splitAtLastTrue}
For an ordered flag word, the last-visit code encodes the index of the last true flag, obtained by a reverse marker scan followed by a binary length computation, or the empty word when no flag is set.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial-time last-visit coding]
\lean{Complexity.clLastCode_native}
\label{Complexity.clLastCode_native}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.comp, Complexity.clLastCode, Complexity.clNative_linear, Complexity.clNative_map, Complexity.clNative_pair, Complexity.clVisitCode, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_id, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_const, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_lengthBits, Turing.FinTM.computesFunInTime_stripLast, Turing.pairDecode, Turing.pairDecode_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode, Turing.splitAtLastTrue}
\difficulty{4}
The function that sends a Boolean word to the code of the index immediately before its
last true entry, with the empty word returned when there is no true entry, is computable
in polynomial time.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Appending a marker]
\lean{Complexity.clLastMarker_step}
\label{Complexity.clLastMarker_step}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.splitAtLastTrue}
\difficulty{2}
For every Boolean word $w$ and Boolean entry $b$, the prefix before the last true entry
of the word obtained by appending $b$ to $w$ is $w$ if $b$ is true, and otherwise is the
prefix before the last true entry of $w$; in either case the prefix is undefined if the
corresponding word has no true entry.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Pure last-match tracker]
\lean{Complexity.clLastIndex}
\label{Complexity.clLastIndex}
\leanok
For a predicate on times and a bound, the tracker scans all indices below the bound in order, replacing its candidate at every match, and returns the last matching index, or nothing when no index matches.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Marker scan and last-match tracker]
\lean{Complexity.clLastIndex_marker}
\label{Complexity.clLastIndex_marker}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clLastIndex, Complexity.clLastMarker_step, Turing.splitAtLastTrue}
\difficulty{3}
Let $P\colon\mathbb{N}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ and let $n\in\mathbb{N}$. The
length of the prefix before the last true entry in the word $(P(0),\ldots,P(n-1))$, when
such an entry exists, and no value otherwise, is the last index below $n$ at which $P$
is true, or is undefined if there is no such index.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Last match as a filtered maximum]
\lean{Complexity.clLastIndex_max}
\label{Complexity.clLastIndex_max}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clLastIndex}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P\colon\mathbb{N}\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ and $n\in\mathbb{N}$. The
last index below $n$ at which $P$ is true, or no value if there is none, equals the
maximum of the set of indices below $n$ at which $P$ is true, with the maximum undefined
for the empty set.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Flag code for a previous visit]
\lean{Complexity.clLastCode_prev}
\label{Complexity.clLastCode_prev}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clLastCode, Complexity.clLastIndex_marker, Complexity.clLastIndex_max, Complexity.clVisitCode, Complexity.prevVisit, Complexity.workPosAt, Turing.FinTM}
\difficulty{2}
Let $M$ be a finite-state binary Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let
$m,t\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $\tau$ be one of its work tapes. Form the Boolean word of
length $t$ whose entry at $s<t$ is true exactly when the head of tape $\tau$, after $s$
steps on the all-zero input of length $m$, is at the same position as after $t$ steps.
The code of the index immediately before the word's last true entry (or the empty word
if there is none) equals the optional-time code of the largest such $s<t$, with the code
empty if no such $s$ exists.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Buffer replay machine]
\lean{Complexity.clReplayTM}
\label{Complexity.clReplayTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM}
A three-state machine with one work tape replays a stored buffer to the physical output: started at the buffer's right blank, it rewinds explicitly to the origin, emits every stored bit left to right, and physically halts on the final blank; no verdict or terminator is added.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Replay configuration]
\lean{Complexity.clReplayCfg}
\label{Complexity.clReplayCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape}
For an input word, an input position, an optional control, a stored buffer, a head cell, and current output, the replay configuration is the one-tape configuration retaining the buffer and the native input head.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Backward rewind of the replay machine]
\lean{Complexity.clReplay_back}
\label{Complexity.clReplay_back}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clReplayCfg, Complexity.clReplayTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x$ and $w$ be Boolean words, let $p$ be an input-head position for $x$, let $out$
be an output word, and let $j$ be a natural number with $j\le |w|$. Starting with the
replay machine in rewind state at work-tape head position $j-1$, it reaches after $j+1$
steps the emitting state with the same buffer $w$, output $out$, and work-tape head at
position zero; the input-head position remains $p$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Forward replay of a buffer suffix]
\lean{Complexity.clReplay_forward}
\label{Complexity.clReplay_forward}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clReplayCfg, Complexity.clReplayTM, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape_nat, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $x,w,out$ be Boolean words, let $p$ be an input-head position for $x$, and let $j$
be a natural number with $j\le |w|$. Starting with the replay machine in its emitting
state, its work-tape head at position $j$, and output $out$, after $|w|-j+1$ steps it
halts with the work-tape head at position $|w|$ and output $out$ followed by the suffix
of $w$ beginning at position $j$; the input-head position remains $p$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Complete Buffer Replay]
\lean{Complexity.clReplay_run}
\label{Complexity.clReplay_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clReplayCfg, Complexity.clReplayTM, Complexity.clReplay_back, Complexity.clReplay_forward, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{3}
Let $x,w,$ and $out$ be finite Boolean words, and let $p$ be an input-head position for
$x$. Starting with the replay machine in its start control, its work tape storing $w$
with the head at cell $|w|$, and output $out$, after $2|w|+3$ steps it is halted, the
head is at cell $|w|$, the buffer remains $w$, and the output is $out$ followed by $w$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Quantitative buffered composition]
\lean{Complexity.clCompute_comp}
\label{Complexity.clCompute_comp}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime.mono, Turing.FinTM.VirtualTag, Turing.FinTM.bufferedCompTM, Turing.FinTM.bufferedComp_start, Turing.FinTM.bufferedSecondCfg, Turing.FinTM.bufferedSecondCfg_run, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.output_length_le, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{4}
Let a machine compute output $y$ from input $x$ within time $a$, and a second machine compute $z$ from $y$ within time $b$. Then the buffered composition of the two machines computes $z$ from $x$ within time $2a + b + 2$; the second machine's contract is needed only on the actual intermediate word.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Selecting one physical tape]
\lean{Complexity.clOneSelect}
\label{Complexity.clOneSelect}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacement, Complexity.clPlacement.ofInverse}
For a chosen tape coordinate, the selection maps that tape to the single local slot and leaves every other tape and head framed.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Attaching a physical replay to a completion]
\lean{Complexity.clOutputTM}
\label{Complexity.clOutputTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clOneSelect, Complexity.clPlacedAction, Complexity.clReplayTM, Turing.Action.mapState, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction}
Given a machine with an absorbing live completion control and a chosen buffer tape, the extended machine runs the original computation unchanged, dispatches once at the first completion, and then replays the chosen buffer to the physical output; the source computation and its startup are untouched before the return.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Returning a buffer with its head at the end]
\lean{Complexity.clOutput_compute}

every input word $x$ and every configuration $c$ of the prepared machine on $x$ whose
state is the copy of $r$ in the prepared machine's state space, one step leaves $c$
unchanged.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Exact runtime for computing query flags]

Let $l,N,W,U$ be natural numbers, let $p,n\in\{0,\ldots,l-1\}$ be distinct, let $r_s(i)$
be a family of bit words, let $y_0,y_1$ be target bit words, and let $v$ be a bit-word
tail. Suppose $|r_s(i)|\le W$ for every $s<N$ and every $i$, $|y_j|\le W$ for each
$j\in\{0,1\}$, and each query word formed from the targets, the stream of packed rows
followed by $v$, and the unary clock of length $N$ has length at most $U$. Then the
finite binary query machine on the packed query argument $a$ halts within
$2|a|+9+(l+5)(3U+7)+N(l(5W+7)+2W+7)$ steps and outputs, in source-time order, the $N$
Boolean flags indicating whether $r_s(p)+y_1=r_s(n)+y_0$, with each word interpreted as
a little-endian binary numeral.

\begin{lemma}[Machine for querying comparison flags]

\difficulty{3}

be a family of bit words indexed by times $s$ and coordinates $i$, let $y_0,y_1$ be
target bit words, and let $v$ be a bit-word tail. Suppose $|r_s(i)|\le W$ for every
$s<N$ and every $i$, $|y_j|\le W$ for each $j\in\{0,1\}$, and each of the $l+5$ query
words formed from the targets, the stream of packed rows followed by $v$, and the unary
clock of length $N$ has length at most $U$. There exist a finite binary Turing machine
$Q$ and natural numbers $c,e$ such that, on the packed query argument, $Q$ outputs in at
most $2(2|a|+9+(l+5)(3U+7)+N(l(5W+7)+2W+7))+c(N+1)^e+2$ steps the optional-time code of
the greatest $s<N$ for which the value of $r_s(p)$ plus the value of $y_1$ equals the
value of $y_0$ plus the value of $r_s(n)$; if no such $s$ exists, it outputs the code
for absence. Here $a$ denotes that packed argument and each word is interpreted as a
little-endian binary numeral.

\begin{definition}[Unary-bounded repetition controller]

Given a clean-call machine with entry and exit controls, the repetition controller tests a protected unary clock, and for each live token executes one complete clean call on the shared argument bank, then dispatches back; a fresh begin phase executes the call's first transition before testing the positive return, so entry and exit controls may coincide. word of length $c\bigl(A(|x|+C(|x|+1)^e+1)^d+1\bigr)^2+1$ is polynomial-time computable.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial-time visit table]

For every finite-state binary Turing machine $M$ and natural numbers $C,e,c,A,d$, the
function that sends a Boolean word $x$ to the table of visit rows for $M,C,e,x$, with
count $c\,(A(|x|+C(|x|+1)^e+1)^d+1)^2+1$, is polynomial-time computable.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Complete packed preparation data]
\lean{Complexity.clPackedRecords}
\label{Complexity.clPackedRecords}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPrepHeader, Complexity.clProducerHorizon, Complexity.clRecords, Complexity.clVisitRows, Turing.FinTM, Turing.pairEncode}
For a source machine, parameters $C, e, c, A, d$, and an instance $x$, the packed record is the nested pair of: the untouched exact arithmetic header of $x$; the inclusive chronological movement-count trajectory over the all-false reference input of length $|x| + C(|x|+1)^e$ at the producer horizon plus one; and the inclusive time-ordered, work-tape-ordered table of canonical last-visit codes.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial-time computability of packed records]
\lean{Complexity.clPackedRecords_native}
\label{Complexity.clPackedRecords_native}
\leanok

\difficulty{1}
For every finite-state Boolean Turing machine $M$ and natural numbers $C,e,c,A,d$, the
function sending each Boolean word $x$ to its packed records is computable in polynomial
time.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial-time production of packed records]
\lean{Complexity.clPackedRecords_machine}
\label{Complexity.clPackedRecords_machine}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPackedRecords, Complexity.clPackedRecords_native, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.ComputesFunInTime, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.MultiTapeTM.output_length_le}
\difficulty{2}
For every finite-state Boolean Turing machine $M$ and natural numbers $C,e,c,A,d$, there
are a finite-state Boolean Turing machine $H$ and natural numbers $a,r$ such that $H$
computes the function sending each word $x$ to its packed records within $a(|x|+1)^r$
steps, and the resulting word has length at most $a(|x|+1)^r$ for every $x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[First halt in a padded run]
\lean{Complexity.clA5_call_first_halt}
\label{Complexity.clA5_call_first_halt}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.Halted, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_of_halt, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_zero}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a deterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean tape symbols, and
state set $S$. For a Boolean input word $x$, a configuration $c$, and $t\in\mathbb{N}$,
suppose $c$ is live and the configuration reached after $t$ steps is halted. Then there
is a time $u$ with $0<u\le t$ such that every configuration at time $v<u$ is live, and
the configuration at time $u$ equals the one at time $t$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Padding an action into a shared bank]
\lean{Complexity.clA5PadAction}
\label{Complexity.clA5PadAction}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Action}
An action on $k$ tapes is padded to a larger bank of $K$ tapes by keeping its input move, output emission, and successor state, applying its writes and moves on the first $k$ tapes, and leaving every additional tape stationary.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Padded module over the shared bank]
\lean{Complexity.clA5PadTM}
\label{Complexity.clA5PadTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clA5PadAction, Turing.FinTM}
For a machine with $k \le K$ tapes, the padded machine on $K$ tapes runs the same control, reading only the first $k$ work symbols and padding each action; all modules can therefore share tape zero and one common bank.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Padded configuration]
\lean{Complexity.clA5PadCfg}
\label{Complexity.clA5PadCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg}
The padded form of a configuration on $k$ tapes is the configuration on $K$ tapes that keeps its state, input position, and output, places its tapes and heads on the first $k$ slots, and leaves every additional tape genuinely blank with head zero.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Padding commutes with an action]
\lean{Complexity.clA5Pad_apply}
\label{Complexity.clA5Pad_apply}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clA5PadAction, Complexity.clA5PadCfg, Turing.Action, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg}
\difficulty{3}
Let $k,K\in\mathbb{N}$, let $S$ be a state set, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let
$a$ be an action on $k$ work tapes and $c$ a configuration on those tapes over input
$x$. Applying the action padded to $K$ tapes to the padded configuration gives exactly
the padding of the configuration obtained by applying $a$ to $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Padded runs match source runs]
\lean{Complexity.clA5Pad_run}
\label{Complexity.clA5Pad_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clA5PadAction, Complexity.clA5PadCfg, Complexity.clA5PadTM, Complexity.clA5Pad_apply, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_comm_of_step, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{4}
Let $M$ be a finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let
$K\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $k\le K$, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on a Boolean
input word $x$. For every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, the padded machine's configuration after $t$
steps from the padded $c$ is the padding of $M$'s configuration after $t$ steps from
$c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Padding canonical seam configurations]
\lean{Complexity.clA5Pad_seam}
\label{Complexity.clA5Pad_seam}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clA5PadCfg, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{3}
Let $k,K\in\mathbb{N}$ with $0<k$, let $S$ be a state set, let $x$ be a Boolean input
word, and let $q\in S$ and $w,o$ be Boolean words. Padding the configuration on input
$x$ with state $q$, the word $w$ on tape zero, blank remaining tapes, and output $o$
yields exactly the corresponding configuration on $K$ tapes with the same state word and
output.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Release wrapper of a clean call]
\lean{Complexity.clA5StopTM}
\label{Complexity.clA5StopTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction}
Given a machine with entry and exit controls, the wrapped machine carries one release flag: it executes the underlying transitions, raising the flag after the first step, and physically halts exactly when the flag is set and the control is the exit; an entry equal to the exit therefore still executes at least one step.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Release-flag configuration]
\lean{Complexity.clA5StopCfg}
\label{Complexity.clA5StopCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg}
A configuration of the underlying machine embeds into the wrapped machine by pairing its control with a release flag; all physical fields, tapes, heads, input position, and output, are unchanged.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[One Step of the Release Wrapper]
\lean{Complexity.clA5Stop_step}
\label{Complexity.clA5Stop_step}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clA5StopCfg, Complexity.clA5StopTM, Turing.Cfg, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step}
\difficulty{3}
Let $C$ be a finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machine with designated entry and exit
states, let $x$ be a Boolean input, and let $c$ be a configuration of $C$ on $x$. If $c$
is live and, whenever the release flag is true, the control state of $c$ is not the
designated exit state, then one step of the release wrapper on the configuration
obtained by adding the flag $b$ to $c$ gives the configuration obtained by adding a true
flag to the one-step successor of $c$ under $C$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Live prefixes of a run]
\lean{Complexity.clA5_live_prefix}
\label{Complexity.clA5_live_prefix}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_of_halt}
\difficulty{2}
Let $M$ be a deterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean tape symbols, and
state set $S$, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $c$ be a configuration on $x$.
If the run from $c$ is live at time $t$, then it is live at every time $u\le t$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Clean Call Halts Under the Release Wrapper]
\lean{Complexity.clA5Stop_clean}
\label{Complexity.clA5Stop_clean}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clA5StopCfg, Complexity.clA5StopTM, Complexity.clA5Stop_step, Complexity.clA5_live_prefix, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_succ_eq_step', Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{5}
Let $C$ be a finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machine, with entry and exit states, and let
$x$, $arg$, $result$, and $out$ be Boolean words. Suppose a call from the seam
configuration with entry state and tape word $arg$ reaches the seam configuration with
exit state and tape word $result$, emitting exactly $out$, after a positive number $t$
of steps. Suppose also that its state is not the exit state at any time strictly between
$0$ and $t$. Then the release wrapper, started with its release flag false at the entry
seam, reaches after $t+1$ steps a halted configuration with release flag true, exit
state, tape word $result$, and output $out$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Control of the five-module host]
\lean{Complexity.CLA5HostState}
\label{Complexity.CLA5HostState}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM}
The host's finite control is either the unique loop anchor or a state of one of the five modules: native input copy, packed-record installation, cursor initialization, emission, and cursor update.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Module return destinations]
\lean{Complexity.clA5HostNext}
\label{Complexity.clA5HostNext}
\leanok
Module zero continues to module one, module one to module two, and module three to module four; modules two and four return to the unique loop anchor.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Entry state of a module]
\lean{Complexity.clA5HostEntry}
\label{Complexity.clA5HostEntry}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CLA5HostState, Turing.FinTM}
For each of the five modules, its entry state inside the host is the module's own start control tagged by its index.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Resolved return of a module]
\lean{Complexity.clA5HostRet}
\label{Complexity.clA5HostRet}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CLA5HostState, Complexity.clA5HostEntry, Complexity.clA5HostNext, Turing.FinTM}
A module's return state is the entry of its successor module when one exists, and the loop anchor otherwise; resolving the return performs no tape operation.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The five-module emission host]
\lean{Complexity.clA5HostTM}
\label{Complexity.clA5HostTM}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CLA5HostState, Complexity.clA5HostEntry, Complexity.clA5HostRet, Complexity.clA5PadTM, Turing.FinTM, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.emitAction}
Over one shared padded work bank, the host runs the five modules through their call chain: the anchor dispatches into the emission module, and each module's transitions are forwarded with halts redirected to the module's resolved return; the clean-call contracts restore all scratch before each next call.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Forwarding a Padded Module Seam]
\lean{Complexity.clA5Host_seam}
\label{Complexity.clA5Host_seam}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CLA5HostState, Complexity.clA5HostRet, Complexity.clA5PadCfg, Complexity.clA5Pad_seam, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.emitCfg, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{3}
Let five Boolean finite Turing machines be given, fix a shared bank of $K$ tapes and a
module index $i$ whose machine has positive tape count. For any input word $x$, stored
word $w$, output prefix $\mathrm{pre}$, output word $\mathrm{out}$, state $q$ of module
$i$, and optional state $s$, forwarding the padded configuration with state $s$ and
output $\mathrm{out}$ yields the canonical shared-bank configuration whose tape-zero
word is $w$, output is $\mathrm{pre}$ followed by $\mathrm{out}$, and state is the
tagged state $s$ when present or the module's resolved return state when absent.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[A Module Call Within the Host]
\lean{Complexity.clA5Host_call}
\label{Complexity.clA5Host_call}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CLA5HostState, Complexity.clA5HostEntry, Complexity.clA5HostRet, Complexity.clA5HostTM, Complexity.clA5Host_seam, Complexity.clA5PadCfg, Complexity.clA5PadTM, Complexity.clA5Pad_run, Turing.Cfg.Halted, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.emitCfg, Turing.emit_run, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{5}
Let $M_0,\ldots,M_4$ be five finite Boolean Turing machines, let $K$ bound each
machine's number of work tapes, and fix a module $i$ with $0<(M_i).k$. Suppose that, on
input $x$ with argument word $\mathrm{arg}$ on tape zero, machine $M_i$ starts in its
initial state, does not halt at any time $v<t$, and at time $t$ is halted with result
word $\mathrm{result}$ on tape zero and output $\mathrm{out}$. Then the host started at
module $i$'s entry with the same argument and output prefix $\mathrm{pre}$ does not
reach the loop anchor at any time $v<t$; at time $t$ it is in module $i$'s resolved
return state, with result word on tape zero and output $\mathrm{pre}$ followed by
$\mathrm{out}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Joining two guarded run segments]
\lean{Complexity.clA5_guard_add}
\label{Complexity.clA5_guard_add}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_add}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a deterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean tape symbols, and
state set $S$, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, let $q\in S$, and let $c,d$ be
configurations on $x$. For $a,b\in\mathbb{N}$, suppose the run from $c$ avoids state $q$
at every time $v<a$, the run from $c$ at time $a$ is $d$, and the run from $d$ avoids
state $q$ at every time $v<b$. Then the run from $c$ avoids state $q$ at every time
$v<a+b$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Uniform clean-module contract]
\lean{Complexity.CLA5Clean}
\label{Complexity.CLA5Clean}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg.Halted, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.stateWord}
A machine satisfies the clean contract for a result map, an emission map, and a budget when it has a positive tape count and, for every native input and argument word, it first halts at some positive time within the budget of the argument length, at the canonical seam holding the result word and having emitted exactly the prescribed chunk.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Release wrapper for clean computations]
\lean{Complexity.clA5Clean_stop}
\label{Complexity.clA5Clean_stop}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CLA5Clean, Complexity.clA5StopTM, Complexity.clA5Stop_clean, Complexity.clA5_call_first_halt, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{3}
Let $C$ be a finite Turing machine, let $entry,exit$ be states of $C$, and let $result$
and $emit$ map binary words to binary words. Let $B:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and suppose
$C$ has a positive number of work tapes. Assume that for every binary input $x$ and
argument word $arg$, there is a time $t\le B(|arg|)$ with $t>0$ such that at every time
$v$ with $0<v<t$ the machine has not reached $exit$, and at time $t$ its configuration
is the seam configuration with state $exit$, tape words encoding $result(arg)$, and
output $emit(arg)$. Then the release wrapper of $C$ satisfies the clean contract for
$result$ and $emit$ with budget $n\mapsto B(n)+1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial bridge bound]
\lean{Complexity.clA5_bridge_bound}
\label{Complexity.clA5_bridge_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $c,A,d,n,\ell$ be natural numbers, and suppose that $\ell \langle A(n+1)^d$. Then
$c\bigl(A(n+1)^d+n+\ell+1\bigr)+1\le \bigl(c(2A+1)+1\bigr)(n+1)^{d+1}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Clean installation of a polynomial-time function]
\lean{Complexity.clA5Clean_install}
\label{Complexity.clA5Clean_install}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CLA5Clean, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.clA5Clean_stop, Complexity.clA5StopTM, Complexity.clA5_bridge_bound, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.FinTM.exists_installCallTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.output_length_le}
\difficulty{4}
Every polynomial-time computable function $f$ on binary words has a finite Turing
machine $M$ and natural numbers $A,d$ such that, for every binary input $x$ and argument
word, the computation first halts at a positive time no greater than $A(n+1)^d$, where
$n$ is the argument length; at that time its tape words encode $f$ of the argument and
its output is empty.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Clean emission of a polynomial-time function]
\lean{Complexity.clA5Clean_emit}
\label{Complexity.clA5Clean_emit}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CLA5Clean, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.clA5Clean_stop, Complexity.clA5StopTM, Complexity.clA5_bridge_bound, Turing.FinTM.computesInTime_iff, Turing.FinTM.exists_emitCallTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.output_length_le}
\difficulty{4}
Every polynomial-time computable function $f$ on binary words has a finite Turing
machine $M$, natural numbers $A,d$, and a clean computation such that for every binary
input $x$ and argument word, the computation first halts at a positive time no greater
than $A(n+1)^d$, where $n$ is the argument length; at that time its tape words encode
the unchanged argument and its output is exactly $f$ of the argument.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Clean Contracts at a Host Call]
\lean{Complexity.clA5Host_clean}
\label{Complexity.clA5Host_clean}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CLA5Clean, Complexity.clA5HostEntry, Complexity.clA5HostRet, Complexity.clA5HostTM, Complexity.clA5Host_call, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{2}
Let $M_0,\ldots,M_4$ be five finite Boolean Turing machines, and suppose their tape
counts are all at most $K$. Fix an index $i$, maps $f,g$ from Boolean words to Boolean
words, and a time-bound function $B$. If $M_i$ has positive tape count and, for every
input word $x$ and argument word $\mathrm{arg}$, halts for the first time at some
positive time $t\le B(|\mathrm{arg}|)$ with canonical seam containing $f(\mathrm{arg})$
and output $g(\mathrm{arg})$, then for every output prefix $\mathrm{pre}$ the host
started at module $i$'s entry with argument $\mathrm{arg}$ avoids the loop anchor before
such a time and reaches its resolved return with tape word $f(\mathrm{arg})$ and output
$\mathrm{pre}$ followed by $g(\mathrm{arg})$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Clean bounded-time input copy]
\lean{Complexity.clA5Copy_clean}
\label{Complexity.clA5Copy_clean}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clA5StopTM, Complexity.clA5Stop_clean, Complexity.clA5_call_first_halt, Complexity.clInputTM, Complexity.clInput_first, Turing.Cfg.Halted, Turing.Cfg.init, Turing.Cfg.ofWords, Turing.FinTM.bufferTape, Turing.MultiTapeTM.initCfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.stateWord}
\difficulty{4}
For every Boolean word $x$, let $D$ be the release-wrapped three-state input copier
described by the machine construction. There is a time $t$ with $0<t\le 2|x|+3$ such
that $D$ has not halted at any time $j<t$, and at time $t$ it is halted in the
configuration whose tape zero stores $x$, whose other work tapes are blank, whose input
head and work-tape heads are at their initial positions, and whose output is empty.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial-time packed-record producer]
\lean{Complexity.clA5Packed_install}
\label{Complexity.clA5Packed_install}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.CLA5Clean, Complexity.clA5Clean_install, Complexity.clPackedRecords, Complexity.clPackedRecords_machine, Turing.FinTM}
\difficulty{1}
For every finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machine $M$ and all $C,e,c,A,d\in\mathbb{N}$,
there are a function $S$ on bit strings and natural numbers $a,r$ such that $M$ has at
least one work tape and the following holds for every input word $x$ and argument word
$u$. Starting with $S(u)$ on the first work tape and all other work tapes blank, the
machine, on input $x$, halts after some positive number $t\le a(|u|+1)^r$ of steps; it
does not halt at any earlier step, and at step $t$ its configuration has output equal to
the empty word and otherwise agrees with the canonical configuration containing the
packed records for $u$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Persistent body word with emission cursor]
\lean{Complexity.clA5Pack}
\label{Complexity.clA5Pack}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPackedRecords, Turing.FinTM, Turing.pairEncode}
For a source machine, parameters, instance $x$, and cursor value $i$, the persistent body word is the pair of the unary cursor of $i$ tokens with the entire unchanged packed producer answer; the original instance remains inside its header.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Clean cursor installation module]
\lean{Complexity.clA5Cursor_install}
\label{Complexity.clA5Cursor_install}
\leanok

\difficulty{1}
There exist a finite Boolean Turing machine $S$ and natural numbers $a,r$ such that $S$
has at least one work tape and, for every Boolean input word $x$ and argument word $v$,
it first halts at some time $t$ satisfying $0<t\le a(|v|+1)^r$. At that time its tape
zero stores the pair encoding of the empty word and $v$, its other work tapes are blank,
its heads are at their initial positions, and its output is empty.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Concrete body module bank]
\lean{Complexity.clA5Modules}
\label{Complexity.clA5Modules}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clA5StopTM, Complexity.clInputTM, Turing.FinTM}
Given install, cursor, emission, and update machines, the five body modules are: the release-wrapped native input copier, the packed-record installer, the cursor installer, the emission module, and the cursor-update module.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Tape bound for the module bank]
\lean{Complexity.clA5Modules_bound}
\label{Complexity.clA5Modules_bound}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clA5Modules, Complexity.clA5StopTM, Complexity.clInputTM, Turing.FinTM}
\difficulty{2}
Let $S,J,E,I$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, with work-tape counts
$k_S,k_J,k_E,k_I$. For each of the five modules formed from the release-wrapped input
copier and these four machines, the number of work tapes is at most $1+k_S+k_J+k_E+k_I$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Polynomial-Time Startup to the First Anchor]
\lean{Complexity.clA5Startup}
\label{Complexity.clA5Startup}

\begin{definition}[Semantics of a one-way transducer]
\lean{Complexity.clA5MapWord}
\label{Complexity.clA5MapWord}
\leanok
For a finite state set with a step function, an optional per-bit emission, and an optional final emission, the transduction of a word processes each bit in order, appending its optional emitted bit and updating the state, and appends the optional final bit at the end; at most one bit is emitted per input bit.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Finite one-way transducer machine]
\lean{Complexity.clA5MapTM}
\label{Complexity.clA5MapTM}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.FinTM}
For a finite state set with step, emission, and finishing functions and a start state, the transducer is a machine with no work tapes that scans its input left to right, emits the per-bit outputs, and halts at the right boundary after the optional final emission.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Scanner frame of the transducer]
\lean{Complexity.clA5MapCfg}
\label{Complexity.clA5MapCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.Cfg}
For an input word, a state, a scanned-prefix length, and an already-emitted output, the scanner frame is the configuration with the input head just past the prefix and no work tapes.
\end{definition}

per-bit output, and an optional final output, and choose a start state. For any bit
strings $x$ and $r$, any prefix $p$ satisfying $x=p r$, any state $q$, and any already
emitted bit string $o$, running the associated transducer machine from the configuration
with input $x$, state $q$, input head just past $p$, and output $o$ for $|r|+1$ steps
halts and leaves output equal to $o$ followed by the transduction of $r$ starting in
state $q$.

\begin{lemma}[Cursor update on packed words]
\lean{Complexity.clA5Next_pack}
\label{Complexity.clA5Next_pack}

\uses{Complexity.clA5Next, Complexity.clA5Pack, Complexity.clA5Stored_exact, Complexity.clHeaderField, Complexity.clHeaderTail, Complexity.clLastRound, Complexity.clProducerHorizon, Turing.FinTM, Turing.pairDecode_pairEncode}
\difficulty{3}
Let $M$ be a Turing machine with a finite state set and Boolean tape alphabet, let
$C,e,c,A,d$ be natural numbers, let $x$ be a finite bit string, and let $i$ be a natural
number. Set $T=c\bigl(A(|x|+C(|x|+1)^e+1)^d+1\bigr)^2$ and $R=|x|+(M.k+3)T+M.k+1$, where
$M.k$ is the number of work tapes of $M$. If $i\le R+1$, then applying the cursor update
to the packed encoding with unary cursor $i$ and data determined by $M,C,e,c,A,d,x$
yields the packed encoding with the same data and unary cursor $\min(i+1,R+1)$; in
particular, the cursor remains at $R+1$ once it reaches that value.
\end{lemma}

$x$ to the little-endian binary representation of this quantity at $n=|x|$ is
polynomial-time computable.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[One round of the five-module host]

\leanok

and $\mathrm{next}$ map Boolean words to Boolean words, and let

with the standard word assignment for $\mathrm{next}(w)$ and output $\mathrm{emit}(w)$;

\end{definition}

at time $t\le T$ evaluates to true on each of the $k$ tapes; and the acceptance
constraint holds at every $t<T$.

\section{Additional declarations}

\begin{definition}[Placement with an exact selector]
\lean{Complexity.clPlacement}
\label{Complexity.clPlacement}
\leanok
For natural numbers $k$ and $l$, a placement consists of an injective map from the $k$
positions to the $l$ positions and a selector assigning to each of the $l$ positions
either no position or one of the $k$ positions. The selector returns position $i$ at
position $j$ exactly when the injective map sends $i$ to $j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Placement from inverse maps]
\lean{Complexity.clPlacement.ofInverse}
\label{Complexity.clPlacement.ofInverse}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacement}
For natural numbers $k,l$, let $f$ map the $k$ positions to the $l$ positions and let
$s$ assign to each of the $l$ positions either no position or one of the $k$ positions.
Suppose $s(f(i))=i$ for every position $i$, and whenever $s(j)=i$, one has $f(i)=j$.
These maps define a placement whose embedding is $f$ and whose selector is $s$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Relabelled placement]
\lean{Complexity.clPlacement.permute}
\label{Complexity.clPlacement.permute}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacement}
For natural numbers $k,l$, let a placement map the $k$ positions injectively into the
$l$ positions, with its exact selector. Relabel the $k$ positions by a bijection from
the $k$ positions to themselves; the resulting placement sends each position through
that bijection and then through the original placement, and its selector applies the
inverse bijection to the original selector's value when that value exists.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Identity placement]
\lean{Complexity.clPlacement.refl}
\label{Complexity.clPlacement.refl}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacement}
For each natural number $k$, the identity placement from the $k$ positions to themselves
sends each position to itself, and its selector returns that position at each input.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Empty placement]
\lean{Complexity.clPlacement.empty}
\label{Complexity.clPlacement.empty}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacement}
For each natural number $l$, the placement from zero positions into the $l$ positions
has the unique map from the empty set as its embedding, and its selector returns no
position at every input.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Disjoint sum of placements]
\lean{Complexity.clPlacement.sum}
\label{Complexity.clPlacement.sum}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacement, Complexity.clPlacement.ofInverse}
Let $k,l,m,n$ be natural numbers, and let one placement map the $k$ positions into the
$l$ positions and another map the $m$ positions into the $n$ positions, each with its
exact selector. Their disjoint sum is a placement from $k+m$ positions into $l+n$
positions: it uses the first placement on the first blocks and the second placement on
the second blocks, with the corresponding selectors on those blocks.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Composition of placements]
\lean{Complexity.clPlacement.comp}
\label{Complexity.clPlacement.comp}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacement}
Let $k,l,m$ be natural numbers, and let a placement from $k$ positions into $l$
positions assign each source position a distinct target position, with a selection map
that identifies exactly the source position placed at any given target. Composing a
placement from $k$ into $l$ with one from $l$ into $m$ gives the placement whose index
map is the composition of the two index maps and whose selection map applies the second
selection and then the first.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Trailing placement]
\lean{Complexity.clPlacement.trailing}
\label{Complexity.clPlacement.trailing}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacement}
For natural numbers $k$ and $l$, the trailing placement of $l$ positions into $k+l$
positions sends each source position to the target position obtained by adding $k$. Its
selection map returns the corresponding source position on those last $l$ target
positions and is undefined on the first $k$ positions.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Keep-last placement]
\lean{Complexity.clKeepLastPlacement}
\label{Complexity.clKeepLastPlacement}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacement, Complexity.clPlacement.empty, Complexity.clPlacement.ofInverse, Complexity.clPlacement.refl, Complexity.clPlacement.sum}
For a natural number $k$, the placement of $k$ positions into $k+1$ positions sends each
source position to the target with the same index. Its selection map identifies those
first $k$ positions and is undefined at the final position.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Lookup in an Injective Placement]
\lean{Complexity.clPlacement_lookup}
\label{Complexity.clPlacement_lookup}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacement}
\difficulty{4}
Let $k,l\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\iota$ be an injective map from the $k$ slots to the $l$
slots, and let a selection rule return slot $i$ exactly when the $l$-slot position is
the image of $i$. For every position $j$ among the $l$ slots, searching the ordered list
of the $k$ slots for the first $i$ with $\iota(i)=j$ returns precisely the selection
rule's value at $j$ (and returns no value when there is no such $i$).
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Placed machine action]
\lean{Complexity.clPlacedAction}
\label{Complexity.clPlacedAction}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacement, Turing.Action, Turing.Action.mapState, Turing.embedEmitTM}
Given a placement of $k$ work tapes into $l$ work tapes, a state map from $S$ to $H$, a
state $q\in S$, and an action of a $k$-tape Boolean machine with state set $S$, the
placed action is the resulting $l$-tape Boolean action obtained by embedding the source
transition at $q$ into the larger tape arrangement and renaming its state by the given
map.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Placed machine configuration]
\lean{Complexity.clPlacedCfg}
\label{Complexity.clPlacedCfg}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacement, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.embedEmitCfg}
Given a placement of $k$ work tapes into $l$ work tapes, a state map from $S$ to $H$,
$l$ tape-content functions and head positions, and a configuration of a $k$-tape Boolean
machine on input $x$, the placed configuration is obtained by embedding that
configuration into the $l$-tape arrangement and renaming its state by the given map.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Formula for a placed action]
\lean{Complexity.clPlacedAction_eq}
\label{Complexity.clPlacedAction_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacedAction, Complexity.clPlacement, Complexity.clPlacement_lookup, Turing.Action}
\difficulty{3}
Let $k,l$ be natural numbers, let $S,H$ be types, and let a placement consist of an
injection from the $k$ source tape indices into the $l$ host tape indices and a selector
that identifies the source index at each occupied host index. Given a state map $S\to
H$, a state $q\in S$, and an action $a$ on the $k$ source tapes, the placed action has
the same input-head movement, output symbol, and successor state mapped into $H$; at
each host tape it uses the source tape action selected by the placement, or writes
nothing and does not move if that host tape is unoccupied.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Formula for a placed configuration]
\lean{Complexity.clPlacedCfg_eq}
\label{Complexity.clPlacedCfg_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacedCfg, Complexity.clPlacement, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.FinTM.controlAction, Turing.embedEmitCfg, Turing.embedEmitCfg_selected_pos, Turing.embedEmitCfg_selected_tape, Turing.embedEmitTM_frame}
\difficulty{5}
Let $k,l$ be natural numbers, let $S,H$ be types, and let a placement consist of an
injection from the $k$ source tape indices into the $l$ host tape indices and a selector
that identifies the source index at each occupied host index. Given a state map $S\to
H$, host tape contents and head positions, and a source configuration $c$, the placed
configuration has state obtained by mapping the state of $c$, the same input-head
position and output as $c$, and on each host tape uses the contents and head position of
the selected source tape when occupied, or the supplied host contents and head position
otherwise.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Action on a placed configuration]
\lean{Complexity.clPlaced_apply}
\label{Complexity.clPlaced_apply}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacedAction, Complexity.clPlacedCfg, Complexity.clPlacement, Turing.Action, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.Cfg.mapState_apply, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.embedEmitCfg, Turing.embedEmitTM, Turing.embedEmitTM_runFrom}
\difficulty{4}
Let $k,l$ be natural numbers, let $S,H$ be types, and let a placement consist of an
injection from the $k$ source tape indices into the $l$ host tape indices and a selector
that identifies the source index at each occupied host index. For any state map $S\to
H$, source state $q$, host tape contents and head positions, source action $a$, and
source configuration $c$, applying the placed version of $a$ to the placed version of
$c$ gives the placed version of the configuration obtained by applying $a$ to $c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Iterated simulation by placed configurations]
\lean{Complexity.clPlaced_run}
\label{Complexity.clPlaced_run}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacedAction, Complexity.clPlacedCfg, Complexity.clPlacement, Turing.Cfg, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom, Turing.MultiTapeTM.runFrom_mapState_of_agreeOn, Turing.embedEmitCfg, Turing.embedEmitTM, Turing.embedEmitTM_runFrom}
\difficulty{3}
Let $k,l$ be natural numbers, let $S,H$ be types, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let a
placement consist of an injection from the $k$ source tape indices into the $l$ host
tape indices and an exact selector for its occupied indices. Suppose the state map $S\to
H$ is injective, and there is a predicate on source states such that, whenever that
predicate holds at a source state $q$, the host transition from its mapped state agrees
on every input symbol and host tape-symbol tuple with the placed action corresponding to
the source transition at $q$. Given host tape contents and head positions, a source
configuration $c$, and a natural number $t$, if every state reached from $c$ at each
time $j<t$ satisfies the predicate whenever that configuration is in a source state,
then running the host machine for $t$ steps from the placed configuration equals placing
the source machine's configuration after $t$ steps.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[One-step simulation from a release state]
\lean{Complexity.clPlaced_release}
\label{Complexity.clPlaced_release}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.clPlacedAction, Complexity.clPlacedCfg, Complexity.clPlaced_apply, Complexity.clPlacement, Turing.Action.apply, Turing.Cfg, Turing.Cfg.inputSymbol, Turing.Cfg.mapState, Turing.Cfg.workTapeSymbols, Turing.MultiTapeTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.step, Turing.embedEmitCfg, Turing.embedEmitCfg_selected_pos, Turing.embedEmitCfg_selected_tape}
\difficulty{5}
Let $k,l$ be natural numbers, let $S,H$ be types, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let a
placement consist of an injection from the $k$ source tape indices into the $l$ host
tape indices and an exact selector for its occupied indices. Suppose source and host
machines have transition functions related as follows: from the host release state, on
every input symbol and tuple of host-tape symbols, the host transition is the placed
action corresponding to the source transition at state $q$, with source tape symbols
read at the placed indices. Then, for any host tape contents and head positions and any
source configuration $c$ whose state is $q$, one host step from the placed configuration
with its state replaced by the release state equals the placement of the source
machine's next configuration.
\end{lemma}
